**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity preservation of delicate soft tissue morphology within a mineralized hard tissue (tooth), with minimal shrinkage—addressing the user’s prior issue with tissue deformation using BoneClear. Among established methods for hard tissues (T07 tier), Ce3D is aqueous-based, preserves endogenous fluorescence (though not required here), and critically minimizes morphological distortion while enabling deep antibody/dye penetration. PGP9.5 is a well-validated pan-neuronal marker in dental pulp that labels intrapulpal nerve fibers from root apex to coronal branches. IB4 (isolectin B4) binds non-myelinated sensory nerve endings and vascular endothelia in pulp, providing complementary structural context without requiring genetic reporters. Both are compatible with Ce3D and avoid nuclear counterstains that do not contribute target-specific signal per domain cautions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:200) and biotinylated IB4 (10 µg/mL) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary reagents: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:300) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated streptavidin (1:500) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 15% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.5% (wt/vol) saponin in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B (50% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.5% (wt/vol) saponin in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-C (75% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.5% (wt/vol) saponin in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Matching Solution (88% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.52) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with fresh Ce3D-Matching Solution (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and high refractive index matching in dense adult mouse brain tissue (~5–12 mm), enabling deep penetration of antibodies and dyes while preserving 3D vascular architecture with minimal distortion. It is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 conjugates and preserves exogenous fluorescent labels better than iDISCO+ or uDISCO. CD31 (PECAM1) is a well-established endothelial-specific marker for both normal and tumor-associated vasculature, while IB4 lectin binds specifically to glycoproteins on endothelial surfaces, providing complementary labeling of the entire vascular network—including fine capillaries at the tumor invasion front. Dual labeling allows robust 3D reconstruction of tumor-vascular spatial relationships critical for assessing perivascular GBM invasion.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigments present)  
2.1 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (anti-CD31)  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody + Lectin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated Isolectin B4 (IB4, 10 µg/mL) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi for long-term storage at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)  
12.2 Mount sample in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D acquisition.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3 + Alexa Fluor 488, CD8 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep, specific labeling of total T cells (via CD3) and cytotoxic T cell subset (via CD8) in a dense, fixed mouse subcutaneous tumor (~8 mm scale). iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for this tissue tier (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM), offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching for deep imaging, with excellent penetration of antibody-conjugated dyes. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched by iDISCO+, so we use directly conjugated Alexa Fluor antibodies—Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are both compatible with iDISCO+ per the knowledge base. Nuclear counterstains like DAPI are avoided as primary markers per constraints; instead, tumor morphology can be inferred from autofluorescence or optional secondary structural staining (not required here). This strategy enables quantitative spatial mapping of T cell subsets across tumor regions without reliance on non-specific dyes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for pigmented tumors)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (if indirect labeling were used—but here we use direct conjugates, so skip to step 6)  

6 Direct Antibody Staining  
6.1 Incubation with anti-CD3 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 in PBT + 5% DMSO + 3% donkey serum) and anti-CD8 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 in same buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
6.2 Wash with PBT + 5% DMSO.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Repeat wash 5 times, each with fresh PBT + 5% DMSO.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3)+Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem involves 3 mm thick, densely fixed human cortical tissue where deep antibody penetration failed with standard aqueous labeling. uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for dense clinical brain blocks (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching that enables deep (>1 mm) antibody penetration. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 conjugates—robust synthetic fluorophores resistant to organic solvents—and supports dual mature neuron labeling: NeuN (nuclear marker of post-mitotic neurons) and MAP2 (dendritic/somatic cytoskeletal marker). This dual-target strategy improves reliability of mature neuron identification in deep layers by co-localizing nuclear and somatodendritic signals. Endogenous fluorescence is not required (no GFP/YFP transgenes in human tissue), so quenching by uDISCO is irrelevant. The protocol integrates extended permeabilization and elevated-temperature antibody incubation to overcome diffusion barriers in fixed human cortex.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for antibody labeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 5% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:250) diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution every 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-labeling Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution every 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in fresh DBE in a light-protected glass vial at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (from *Lycopersicon esculentum*) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 for functional perfused vasculature; anti-CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibody for endothelial structural morphology]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for lipid- and pigment-rich tissues like placenta (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tier), offering strong delipidation, deep dye/antibody penetration, and excellent preservation of exogenous fluorophores including Alexa Fluor dyes and lectin conjugates. It maintains high signal-to-noise for both vascular lumen labeling (via intravascular lectin perfusion) and immunostained endothelial markers. Lectin-AF647 binds specifically to glycocalyx on luminal endothelial surfaces of perfused vessels, directly reporting functional perfusion status, while CD31 immunostaining reveals total endothelial architecture regardless of flow—enabling precise spatial comparison of perfused vs. structurally present vessels in labyrinth, trophoblast-associated, and marginal zones. FDISCO’s compatibility with both AF488 and AF647 ensures dual-channel integrity without quenching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion-Based Functional Vessel Labeling (performed *before* fixation if live perfusion possible; otherwise, post-fixation vascular filling via microinjection or passive incubation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50 µg/mL *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 in PBS, gently agitated to ensure vascular access.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

2 Immunostaining for Endothelial Structure  
2.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Blocking with 5% normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
2.4 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
2.6 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation and Bleaching  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
4.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed)  
5.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Organic Solvent Transition  
6.1 Incubation with 1:1 mixture of methanol and dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112392) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer sample to fresh ECi in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage at RT, protected from light)  
8.2 Mount in ECi-filled chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy; no additional mounting medium required.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires tracing two distinct somatosensory pathways through a large, lipid-rich CNS sample (3 cm spinal cord + thalamus + cortex). Lipophilic carbocyanine dyes DiI and DiD are ideal for long-range axonal tracing, stably incorporating into membranes without requiring genetic manipulation or antibody penetration. uDISCO is selected because it is specifically validated for long-range projection mapping in whole-mount CNS tissues up to several centimeters, provides strong delipidation for deep clearing of dense neural tissue, preserves DiI/DiD fluorescence robustly, achieves high refractive index matching for light-sheet imaging, and completes clearing in days rather than weeks. Aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS) offer poorer lipid removal for such large samples and slower clearing kinetics, while other solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+) show comparable performance but uDISCO demonstrates superior signal retention for lipophilic tracers in extended spinal-thalamocortical circuits. Nuclear counterstains (e.g., DAPI) are avoided as primary labels per constraints; if needed for registration, they may be added minimally post-clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigment present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (if bleaching performed)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Store samples immersed in 100% DBE in glass vials protected from light at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
6.2 Mount cleared samples in DBE-filled imaging chambers compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for dual-channel (DiI: Ex/Em ~549/565 nm; DiD: Ex/Em ~644/665 nm) 3D acquisition.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-Ki67–Alexa Fluor 568, Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a rapid, high-clearing-power solvent-based method compatible with exogenous dyes and antibodies, ideal for dense 1–5 mm brain organoids. It preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes and enables robust cytoarchitectural delineation (Phalloidin–AF647 for F-actin, a valid structural marker for brain organoid integrity) and proliferation assessment (anti-Ki67–AF568, a target-specific marker for proliferating nuclei). FDISCO minimizes quenching compared to iDISCO+, supports deep penetration in fixed organoids, and achieves RI matching suitable for light-sheet/confocal imaging within days—critical for high-throughput applications. Hoechst was removed because nuclear counterstains (DAPI/Hoechst/PI) are not target-specific markers for either "大脑类器官整体" or "增殖细胞核" per protocol requirements; total cell density can be inferred from structural labeling and Ki67+ nuclei without violating target-specificity rules.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-Clearing Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody anti-Ki67 (1:200 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) + Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100) in blocking buffer (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 2 hours, protected from light)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared from 30% H₂O₂ stock) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing antibody boost – skip if signal sufficient)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Dehydration (repeat after rehydration if used)  
5.1 Incubation with 20% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)  

6 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% ethyl cinnamate (ECi) (Sigma-Aldrich, 112372) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer organoids to glass vials with fresh ECi (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage at RT, protected from light)  
7.2 Mount in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin–Alexa Fluor 555, anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)–Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for dense mouse soft tissues (e.g., skeletal muscle) of 5–20 mm size, offering strong delipidation and deep dye/antibody penetration required for intact NMJ imaging. It efficiently clears myelinated and lipid-rich regions while preserving fine axonal and postsynaptic structures. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses exogenous, covalent or high-affinity probes: alpha-bungarotoxin directly and specifically labels AChR clusters at the postsynaptic membrane; anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) robustly labels motor axons and nerve terminals; Phalloidin provides F-actin reference of myofibers without interfering with NMJ-specific signals. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 555, 647, 488) are compatible with iDISCO+ based on method–fluorophore compatibility data. The protocol integrates labeling before dehydration to ensure optimal probe penetration.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-clearing Immunolabeling and Staining  
1.1 Wash fixed muscle in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST) three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.2 Block in blocking buffer (PBST + 5% normal goat serum + 0.2% Triton X-100). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody: anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500 in blocking buffer). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly in PBST six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
1.5 Incubate simultaneously with:  
  - alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (1 µg/mL in PBST),  
  - Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 in PBST),  
  - secondary antibody: anti-mouse IgG–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 in PBST).  
(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.6 Wash in PBST six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume of 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes of methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

4 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Dehydration (post-rehydration, if step 4 performed)  
5.1 Repeat steps 2.1–2.6 exactly as above. (Temperature: RT, Time: as specified in Step 2)  

6 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.5 Transfer sample to fresh 100% DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Store cleared sample immersed in DBE at RT in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 1 week)  
7.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional coverslipping. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (functional perfused vasculature) + CD31/PECAM1 + Alexa Fluor 647 (total endothelial network)]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method established for dense adult mouse brain tissue (5–12 mm scale), offering strong delipidation power, deep antibody/dye penetration, and excellent preservation of both structural morphology and fluorescence from synthetic dyes like Alexa Fluor 647 and lectin conjugates. Critically, FDISCO preserves lectin-based labeling of intravascularly perfused vessels—enabling discrimination between functional (perfused) and non-perfused or collapsed vessels—while allowing robust immunostaining for CD31 to map the complete endothelial architecture. This dual-labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goal of comparing vascular density, integrity, and perfusion status across tumor core, invasive margin, and adjacent parenchyma. FDISCO’s compatibility with both lectin and Alexa Fluor 647 (per knowledge base) ensures high signal-to-noise 3D imaging of vascular networks in thick glioma specimens.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion-Based Vascular Labeling (if not already performed in vivo)  
1.1 Intracardiac perfusion with 0.9% NaCl (10 mL, RT) followed by 20 µg/mL DyLight 649-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin in PBS (5 mL, RT, 5 min flow). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)  
1.2 Post-fixation with 4% PFA in PBS (pH 7.4) for 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Tissue Preparation  
2.1 Dissect glioma-containing brain block (~8 × 6 × 4 mm) and post-fix in 4% PFA/PBS for additional 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Wash 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Immunostaining for Total Endothelium  
3.1 Block in PBST + 5% normal goat serum + 0.02% sodium azide for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubate with rat anti-mouse CD31 primary antibody (1:200 in blocking buffer). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
3.3 Wash 5 × 12 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  
3.4 Incubate with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 in blocking buffer). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.5 Wash 5 × 12 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 vol 30% H₂O₂ : 5 vol MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Wash 2 × 1 hour in 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

6 Rehydration (for optional nuclear counterstain; omitted here per caution)  
*(Skipped to avoid DAPI/Hoechst interference with vascular quantification)*  

7 Organic Solvent Transition  
7.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Transfer to fresh 100% ECi for long-term storage and imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

9 Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Mount sample in glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with ECi. Seal with coverslip and nail polish. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or store at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-HCN4 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 568, Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for dense, lipid-rich organs like the intact mouse heart (15–20 mm), offering strong delipidation, high refractive index matching (~1.56), and excellent preservation of exogenous fluorescent dyes including Alexa Fluor conjugates. It is compatible with all selected fluorophores and enables deep penetration of antibodies into thick cardiac tissue. HCN4 is a well-established marker for sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodal pacemaker cells; Cntn2 (Contactin-2) specifically labels Purkinje fibers in the ventricular conduction system; Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 binds F-actin to reveal cardiomyocyte orientation as a structural scaffold without interfering with conduction-specific signals. This combination fulfills the requirement for target-specific labeling of both nodal and Purkinje components while enabling spatial correlation with myocardial architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigment present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh: 1 part 30% H₂O₂ + 5 parts methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 10% (wt/vol) Dextran sulfate (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution: anti-HCN4 (1:200), anti-Cntn2 (1:200) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (wt/vol) Dextran sulfate (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies and Phalloidin in blocking solution: donkey anti-rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti-goat IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500), Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (wt/vol) Dextran sulfate (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)

**Chosen Labeling:** [C-FoS + Alexa Fluor 488, Npas4 (IEGs) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires distinguishing two immediate early gene (IEG)-expressing neuronal subpopulations (c-Fos and Npas4) across the entire adult mouse brain at single-cell resolution. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for whole adult mouse brains (T04 tier), offering strong delipidation, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes—critical for robust immunolabeling of nuclear IEG targets. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in iDISCO+, so direct immunostaining with Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 conjugates ensures high signal-to-noise and spectral separability. iDISCO+ also achieves high refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet imaging, with relatively fast processing compared to aqueous methods.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Storage  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) overnight.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12–16 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.3 Store in PBST at 4 ℃ until processing (max 1 week).  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

3 Bleaching (optional but recommended for endogenous pigment removal)  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Permeabilization and Blocking  
5.1 Incubation with PBST containing 20% (vol/vol) DMSO and 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Primary Antibody Staining  
6.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-c-Fos (1:500) and anti-Npas4 (1:500) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (PBST + 5% donkey serum + 0.2% heparin + 1% DMSO).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

7 Washing  
7.1 Wash with PBST + 0.2% heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 × 24 hours, with buffer changes every 24 hours)  

8 Secondary Antibody Staining  
8.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, gentle shaking)  

9 Post-staining Washes  
9.1 Wash with PBST + 0.2% heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 × 24 hours, protected from light)  

10 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2–4 hours, protected from light)  

13 Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Transfer cleared brain into a glass imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The goal requires high-fidelity 3D mapping of neuronal somata and processes throughout the intact adult mouse brain—a large, lipid-rich, and optically dense sample. uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for whole adult mouse brains, offering strong delipidation, deep antibody penetration, high refractive index matching (~1.52), and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in uDISCO, so we use immunolabeling with robust pan-neuronal markers: NeuN for neuronal nuclei/somata and β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) for axons/dendrites. Both are well-validated, target-specific structural markers for neurons, and their conjugation to Alexa Fluor 647 and 488 ensures signal stability and compatibility with uDISCO’s organic solvent environment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for endogenous pigment reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in antibody dilution buffer (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS): anti-NeuN (1:200) and anti-β-III Tubulin (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 five more times (total 6 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies diluted in antibody dilution buffer: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Post-immunostaining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 five more times (total 6 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store cleared brain immersed in DBE in a glass vial, sealed, and protected from light at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 488, MBP+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for long CNS segments (15–80 mm), offering strong delipidation power, deep antibody penetration, and high refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet imaging of intact spinal cords. It preserves tissue geometry better than other organic solvent methods for tubular structures and enables robust long-range axonal tracing. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in uDISCO, so we use immunolabeling with Alexa Fluor dyes—both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are fully compatible with uDISCO. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) labels all neuronal processes (including regenerating fibers), while myelin basic protein (MBP) marks mature/retained myelinated axons, enabling spatial comparison of regenerative vs. preserved fiber populations across injury zones.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for endogenous pigment reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, e.g., BioLegend 801201, 1:500) and anti-MBP (e.g., Abcam ab7349, 1:250) diluted in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Post-labeling Washing  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 four more times (total 5 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 ratio).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) BABB (1:2).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh BABB (1:2) and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [C-FoS + Alexa Fluor 488, Npas4 (IEGs) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The original CUBIC protocol failed due to insufficient delipidation and poor penetration in dense adult mouse whole brain, leading to heterogeneous transparency and weak deep-tissue signal. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for T04_WHOLE_MOUSE_BRAIN_5_12MM samples, offering strong delipidation, high refractive index matching, and excellent antibody penetration—critical for detecting nuclear immediate early gene (IEG) products like c-Fos and Npas4 across the entire brain. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 conjugated antibodies, which are robust, photostable, and validated for iDISCO+. Using two distinct IEG markers (c-Fos and Npas4) enables discrimination of functionally distinct activated neuron subpopulations without relying on non-specific pan-neuronal labels or nuclear counterstains that lack activation specificity.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for adult brain to reduce autofluorescence)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-c-Fos (e.g., Santa Cruz sc-52, 1:500) and anti-Npas4 (e.g., Cell Signaling #13496, 1:250) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 three more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 three more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-resolution 3D reconstruction of axonal trajectories across a 15-mm-long, lipid-rich spinal cord segment containing injury-induced structural complexity. uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for long CNS tracts (T06 tier), offering strong delipidation, deep antibody/dye penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in uDISCO, so we use immunolabeling with β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)—a pan-axonal marker that robustly labels both intact and regenerating axons. Alexa Fluor 488 is fully compatible with uDISCO, ensuring signal retention through dehydration and refractive index matching. Lectin (IB4) was removed from labeling due to marker-level cautions against its use with β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) and other pan-neuronal markers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for spinal cord pigmentation)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) mouse monoclonal antibody (1:500) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times with fresh buffer, changing every 2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Total Time: 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times with fresh buffer, changing every 2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Total Time: 12 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE in light-protected glass vial at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
12.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, avoiding air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Neurofilament-H (NF-H) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-resolution 3D visualization of both regenerating/reshaping axons and residual mature axon tracts across a 15-mm-long, lipid-rich spinal cord segment. uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for long CNS tracts (tier T06_LONG_CNS_OR_TUBULAR_15_80MM), offering strong delipidation, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in uDISCO, so we use immunolabeling: β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) labels all neuronal processes including nascent/regenerating fibers, while Neurofilament-H (NF-H)—a high-molecular-weight neurofilament subunit enriched in mature, stable axons—serves as a structural marker for surviving/resilient axon bundles. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are both highly compatible with uDISCO and enable dual-channel discrimination of dynamic vs. stable axonal populations.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for spinal cord to reduce autofluorescence)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Neurofilament-H (NF-H, clone SMI-32 or equivalent, 1:400) diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE in airtight glass vial protected from light at RT until imaging by light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for long CNS segments (T06 tier), offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for deep imaging of dense spinal cord tissue. It preserves tissue integrity better than electrophoresis-based methods (e.g., CLARITY variants), avoiding mechanical fragmentation during processing—critical for maintaining spatial continuity across the injury epicenter and adjacent regions. Although uDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 568 and 647 conjugates. The dual-labeling strategy targets pan-neuronal cytoskeletal structures: β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) labels all axons (including regenerating fibers), while MAP2 marks dendrites and somata, enabling clear distinction between axonal trajectories and neuronal cell bodies. This combination supports long-range axon tracing, assessment of fiber continuity across the lesion, and spatial correlation between regenerating axons and preserved neural architecture—all without introducing non-listed fluorophores or markers.

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 647, DiI]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity visualization of long-range axonal projections across the entire CNS (35–40 mm) with clear distinction between specific labeled pathways and endogenous fiber architecture. uDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for whole-body or long CNS samples, offering strong delipidation, deep dye penetration, and compatibility with lipophilic tracers (e.g., DiI) and far-red fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor 647). Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in uDISCO, so we avoid GFP/YFP reporters and instead use DiI (injected pre-fixation to label specific cortical projection neurons) combined with pan-axonal immunostaining against β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 to reveal the global axonal scaffold. This dual-labeling strategy enables unambiguous identification of the DiI-labeled projection against the background of all axons, while uDISCO’s high refractive index matching (~1.52) supports deep light-sheet imaging with minimal scattering.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if tissue pigmentation present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining (for β-III Tubulin)  
3.1 Rehydration: sequential incubation in 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
3.2 Permeabilization and blocking: incubation with PBST (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100) + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody diluted 1:500 in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  
3.4 Wash with PBST (3 changes, 24 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 diluted 1:300 in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  
4.2 Wash with PBST (3 changes, 24 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

5 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Delipidation  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) BABB (1:2).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh BABB (1:2) for long-term storage at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
8.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in BABB-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation

10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching

11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 488, MBP+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D visualization of long-range corticospinal projections across the entire CNS (≈40 mm), necessitating a clearing method with strong delipidation power, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with structural labeling of both axons (β-III Tubulin) and myelin (MBP). uDISCO is established for whole-body and long-CNS samples, provides excellent transparency in lipid-rich neural tissue, and preserves Alexa Fluor dyes effectively. Using TUJ1 (pan-neuronal axonal marker) reveals all projection fibers including corticospinal tracts, while MBP staining delineates myelinated tracts to assess spatial relationships between labeled projections and endogenous white matter architecture. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are avoided due to quenching in solvent-based methods; instead, robust Alexa Fluor–conjugated secondary antibodies ensure signal stability through dehydration and high-RI matching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for CNS pigmentation)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 5% (wt/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, e.g., BioLegend 801201, 1:500) and anti-MBP (e.g., Abcam ab7349, 1:250) diluted in PBST + 5% NGS + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five more times (total 6 washes over 24 hours).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500) in PBST + 5% NGS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-Labeling Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five more times (total 6 washes over 24 hours).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE in glass vial protected from light at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)
