**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D mapping of amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques across the entire 5XFAD mouse brain, necessitating deep antibody penetration, strong lipid removal for optical clarity in dense tissue, and compatibility with quantitative volumetric imaging. iDISCO+ is an established organic solvent–based clearing method optimized for whole adult mouse brains (~10 mm scale), offering rapid, high-clearing power with minimal residual autofluorescence—critical for detecting sparse Aβ deposits. It supports robust immunolabeling with covalently conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes, which are highly compatible and resistant to quenching during dehydration and delipidation. We select 6E10 (anti-Aβ1–16 monoclonal antibody) labeled with Alexa Fluor 647 for specific, high-contrast detection of Aβ plaques. NeuN, a pan-neuronal marker, does not specifically label Aβ plaques and violates the requirement for target-specific labeling; thus, it is excluded. This strategy ensures pathological specificity without relying on endogenous fluorescence (which iDISCO+ quenches).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) NaN₃.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibody diluted in blocking solution: anti-6E10 (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 0.2% (wt/vol) NaN₃.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two additional times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibody diluted in blocking solution: donkey anti-mouse IgG1 Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500, for 6E10).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-Staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 0.2% (wt/vol) NaN₃.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two additional times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (Post-Labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store cleared brain immersed in DBE in light-protected glass vial at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
12.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D acquisition.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 647, DiI]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires long-range axonal tracing across a 35–40 mm intact CNS with minimal morphological distortion and strong fluorescence retention in deep tissue. uDISCO is established for whole-body and long CNS samples (T06 tier), provides high clearing power for lipid-rich neural tissue, enables deep antibody/dye penetration, and preserves DiI and Alexa Fluor 647 signals—both compatible per method-fluorophore compatibility data. Endogenous FPs are avoided due to quenching in solvent-based methods; instead, DiI (lipophilic tracer for specific long-range projections) and pan-axonal β-III Tubulin immunostaining with Alexa Fluor 647 (for global axon network reference) provide complementary, stable labeling. This dual-labeling strategy allows discrimination of target projections (DiI) from the endogenous axonal scaffold (TUJ1-AF647), fulfilling the requirement to analyze continuity, branching, and termination without introducing extraneous markers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (critical for CNS pigment removal and uniform clearing)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (β-III Tubulin)  
5.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody diluted 1:500 in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

6 Washing after Primary Antibody  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (H+L) diluted 1:300 in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  

8 Washing after Secondary Antibody  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Post-staining Dehydration  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 DiI Tracer Application (post-clearing labeling for specific projection tracing)  
11.1 Under stereomicroscope, inject DiI crystals (1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate) into the region of interest in the cortex using fine glass micropipette.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate application)  
11.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) DCM containing 0.1 mg/mL DiI (pre-dissolved in DCM).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, gentle rotation)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
12.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) tert-butanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
12.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.4 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for final RI matching.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

13 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 + Alexa Fluor 488, 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for whole adult mouse brains (5–12 mm scale) with high lipid content and dense pathology like Aβ plaques. It enables deep antibody penetration, strong delipidation for high transparency, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647—both robust dyes that survive organic solvent processing and provide spectrally distinct signals for dual-channel validation of Aβ deposits. Using two well-validated anti-Aβ monoclonal antibodies (6E10 targeting Aβ<sub>1–16</sub>, 4G8 targeting Aβ<sub>17–24</sub>) labeled with non-overlapping fluorophores allows precise spatial comparison of plaque recognition across cortical and hippocampal regions without reliance on endogenous fluorescence (which iDISCO+ quenches). This strategy ensures target specificity, minimal cross-reactivity, and quantitative 3D co-localization analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional but recommended for AD brain with heme-rich microhemorrhages)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (wt/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibody mix: 6E10 (1:500) and 4G8 (1:500) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (wt/vol) NGS + 0.02% (wt/vol) NaN₃.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibody mix: anti-mouse IgG1 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and anti-mouse IgG2b conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (wt/vol) NGS + 0.02% (wt/vol) NaN₃.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-Labeling Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

It enables deep antibody penetration, strong delipidation for high transparency, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647—both robust dyes that survive organic solvent processing and provide spectrally distinct signals for dual-channel validation of Aβ deposits. Using two well-validated anti-Aβ monoclonal antibodies (6E10 targeting Aβ<sub>1–16</sub>, 4G8 targeting Aβ<sub>17–24</sub>) labeled with non-overlapping fluorophores allows precise spatial comparison of plaque recognition across cortical and hippocampal regions without reliance on endogenous fluorescence (which iDISCO+ quenches). **Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 / 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 647, Congo red + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for whole adult mouse brains (T04 tier), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for detecting sparse, deep Aβ plaques in 5XFAD models. It preserves Alexa Fluor 568/647 fluorescence effectively while quenching endogenous FPs (irrelevant here as labeling is antibody/dye-based). The dual-target strategy uses 6E10/4G8 (well-validated anti-Aβ monoclonal antibodies) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 for high-specificity immunodetection, and Congo red—a classic amyloid-binding dye—conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 to provide orthogonal, conformation-dependent labeling that complements epitope-based detection. Both fluorophores are compatible with iDISCO+, enabling mutual validation of plaque identity, improved signal-to-noise in deep tissue, and robust 3D quantification across cortical and hippocampal regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Bleaching  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Rehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Blocking and Primary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 3% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: 6E10 (1:500) and 4G8 (1:500) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine, 6% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Washing after Primary Antibody  
4.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Congo Red Co-labeling  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibody (anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, 1:500) and Congo red conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (50 µg/mL) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Washing after Secondary Antibody  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Transfer to fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for adult mouse brain tissue (5–12 mm scale) with high lipid content and dense tumor architecture. It provides strong delipidation and deep dye penetration while preserving the fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes—critical for dual-channel vascular imaging. Unlike iDISCO+, FDISCO maintains compatibility with both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, enabling robust co-labeling of endothelial lumens (via Lectin) and blood-brain barrier tight junctions (via Claudin-5). Lectin perfusion or post-fixation labeling reliably fills functional vasculature, including in tumor regions, while anti-Claudin-5 reveals barrier integrity loss at single-vessel resolution. FDISCO’s high refractive index matching (~1.52) supports deep light-sheet imaging of the entire 8×6×5 mm tumor-containing block with minimal distortion, fulfilling the requirement for spatial comparison of vascular morphology and barrier status across tumor core, margin, and adjacent parenchyma.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigment present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for antibody/dye labeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Co-labeling  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-Claudin-5 (1:200) + biotinylated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin (10 µg/mL) in PBT + 5% serum + 0.02% sodium azide.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Wash with PBT (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Labeling  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) + streptavidin Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBT + 5% serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-labeling Washes  
8.1 Wash with PBT (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
8.2 Wash with PBS (2 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 + Alexa Fluor 488, 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a solvent-based clearing method established for whole adult mouse brains (5–12 mm), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for dense amyloid-laden AD tissue. It achieves high transparency with minimal residual autofluorescence while preserving Aβ plaque morphology. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is irrelevant here as we use exogenous immunolabeling. The dual-antibody strategy (6E10 targeting Aβ<sub>1–16</sub>, 4G8 targeting Aβ<sub>17–24</sub>) provides orthogonal validation of amyloid deposits, minimizing false positives from lipofuscin or non-specific aggregates. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 are fully compatible with iDISCO+ and offer spectrally distinct, photostable signals ideal for 3D quantification across large volumes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional but recommended for AD brain to reduce heme/lipofuscin background)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-6E10 (BioLegend, 1:500) and anti-4G8 (BioLegend, 1:500) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse IgG1 Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-mouse IgG2b Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 2:1 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store cleared brain in 100% DBE at RT in the dark until imaging. Mount in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for adult mouse brain and tumor tissue, offering strong delipidation power for dense samples (~8 mm scale), deep antibody/dye penetration, and excellent preservation of exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor dyes. It maintains high tissue transparency with minimal autofluorescence and is compatible with both Lectin (for pan-endothelial labeling of perfused and non-perfused vasculature) and Claudin-5 (a tight junction protein critical for blood-brain barrier integrity). This dual-labeling strategy enables simultaneous 3D mapping of vascular architecture (Lectin) and endothelial barrier continuity (Claudin-5), directly addressing the scientific goal of correlating tumor invasion paths with vascular co-option, remodeling, and barrier disruption. FDISCO’s compatibility with Alexa Fluor 488/647 ensures bright, stable signals for high-resolution light-sheet imaging across tumor core, invasive front, and normal parenchyma.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for GBM autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Claudin-5 primary antibody (e.g., 1:200 in PBST + 5% serum) and fluorescently conjugated Lectin (e.g., Isolectin B4 from Griffonia simplicifolia, Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated, 1:100 in same buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Final extended wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Dehydration (post-staining)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol mixture, RI ≈ 1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with fresh BABB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh BABB for long-term storage at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
10.2 Mount in BABB-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional steps.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for adult mouse brain tissue with high lipid content and dense tumor regions. It provides strong delipidation and deep dye penetration while preserving exogenous dye-labeled structures such as vasculature and tight junctions. Unlike CUBIC (which caused severe morphological disruption in GBM tissue), FDISCO minimizes swelling and maintains structural integrity of both tumor parenchyma and delicate vascular networks. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) robustly labels perfused and non-perfused vasculature in fixed tissue and is compatible with FDISCO when conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647. Claudin-5, a key tight junction protein of the blood-brain barrier, is best detected via immunostaining with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated secondary antibodies; FDISCO preserves this epitope and fluorophore signal. Both dyes are explicitly marked as compatible with FDISCO in the knowledge base, enabling reliable 3D assessment of vascular continuity, density, branching, and barrier integrity across tumor core, margin, and adjacent brain.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary and Secondary Antibody Staining (for Claudin-5)  
2.1 Incubation with anti-Claudin-5 primary antibody (1:200 in blocking solution).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
2.2 Washing with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (3 changes, 24 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)  
2.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rat or anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 in blocking solution).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
2.4 Washing with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (3 changes, 24 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)  

3 Lectin Vascular Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin, 50 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Washing with PBS (3 changes, 12 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours total)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP) in sparse neurons while resolving fine dendritic morphology. Solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) quench endogenous FPs and are unsuitable. Among aqueous, FP-friendly clearing methods established for 3 mm brain blocks (T02_THICK_SLICE_0P5_3MM), MACS offers strong delipidation with minimal fluorescence loss, excellent compatibility with both endogenous GFP and antibody-conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes, and preserves tissue geometry without significant shrinkage. MAP2 is a well-established dendritic marker that complements sparse GFP+ neuron labeling by enhancing visualization of dendritic arborization and local projection patterns, enabling robust 3D morphometric analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody against MAP2 (mouse anti-MAP2, 1:500 dilution in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500 dilution in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBST, 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methyldiethanolamine (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate imaging (RI ≈ 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed for imaging)  
3.2 For long-term storage, keep sample immersed in MACS-R2 at 4 ℃ in the dark. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 6 months)  
3.3 Prior to re-imaging after storage, equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R2 at RT for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP) in 3 mm mouse brain blocks over long-term storage, while complementing sparse neuronal morphology with a structural dendritic marker. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method established for thick brain slices (0.5–3 mm), preserves endogenous GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence without quenching, enables deep antibody penetration, and causes minimal tissue distortion—critical for accurate dendritic arbor reconstruction. Although MAP2 is a pan-dendritic marker and not subtype-specific, it is explicitly listed as a valid candidate marker for both "神经元(通用)" and "CA1 树突/树突棘结构辅助" targets per the knowledge base, and its use is justified here for structural labeling of dendrites in CA1. Conjugation to Alexa Fluor 488 ensures bright, photostable signal that complements weak endogenous GFP and remains stable during 6-month storage in MACS-RI matching solution. Alexa Fluor 488 is fully compatible with both MAP2 and the MACS method.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody anti-MAP2 (1:500 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:800 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue to fresh MACS-R2 in glass vial with airtight seal (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)  
3.2 Store protected from light at 4 ℃ for up to 6 months; equilibrate to RT for 2 hours before imaging.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample consists of fixed 3 mm mouse brain blocks with weak endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP/YFP) that must be preserved for long-term storage and repeated imaging. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that robustly preserves endogenous fluorescence (including GFP), enables deep antibody penetration in thick tissue slices, minimizes morphological distortion, and uses low-toxicity reagents—making it ideal for longitudinal studies requiring structural fidelity over 6 months. To complement sparse endogenous GFP-labeled neurons and resolve dendritic arborization, we co-label with anti-MAP2 (a dendrite-enriched pan-neuronal structural marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, which is fully compatible with MACS and provides high-contrast dendritic skeleton information without interfering with GFP signal.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or mouse monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing: 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:1000 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing: 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Transfer samples into fresh MACS-R2 in glass vials with airtight PTFE-lined caps (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)  
3.2 Store at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 6 months; avoid freeze-thaw cycles  
3.3 Prior to imaging, equilibrate samples in fresh MACS-R2 at RT for 2 hours to ensure optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The sample contains weak endogenous GFP signal that must be preserved over 6 months, ruling out solvent-based clearing methods (e.g., uDISCO, iDISCO+) that quench fluorescent proteins. Among aqueous, FP-compatible methods established for 3 mm brain blocks (MACS, Ce3D, ScaleS, FOCM), MACS offers the best balance of rapid clearing (~1–2 days), excellent endogenous FP preservation, deep antibody penetration, minimal tissue distortion, and compatibility with long-term storage in high-RI aqueous media. For structural补全 of sparse neurons, MAP2 is a well-validated dendritic marker that labels proximal and distal dendrites without requiring subtype specificity, and Alexa Fluor 488 is fully compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from GFP while amplifying weak dendritic signals. This dual-labeling strategy preserves the original reporter identity (GFP) while robustly reinforcing dendritic morphology for quantitative analysis after archival storage.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or mouse monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:800 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0: 20% (vol/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue to final storage medium: MACS-R2 supplemented with 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide (NaN₃) to prevent microbial growth (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite up to 6 months)  
3.2 Store samples in amber glass vials sealed with parafilm to minimize light exposure and evaporation (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 months)  

4 Imaging Preparation (after storage)  
4.1 Equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R2 at RT for 2 hours prior to imaging to restore optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Mount in glass-bottom dish filled with MACS-R2 for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a high-clearing-power solvent-based method established for dense human clinical brain tissue (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), enabling deep antibody penetration into 3 mm thick slices—addressing the core failure of superficial-only labeling. It efficiently removes lipids while maintaining structural integrity sufficient for cortical lamination analysis. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in uDISCO, so robust synthetic fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/647) conjugated to well-validated pan-mature-neuronal markers NeuN (nuclear) and MAP2 (somatic/dendritic) provide complementary, non-overlapping signals for reliable 3D neuron identification, counting, and density mapping. Both Alexa Fluor dyes are fully compatible with uDISCO, and dual labeling mitigates false negatives in deep tissue. Antibody incubation is integrated post-fixation but pre-dehydration to maximize penetration before lipid removal.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Primary Antibody Incubation  
1.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-NeuN (1:500) and rabbit anti-MAP2 (1:500) diluted in PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 5% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 (3 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 5% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

4 Post-labeling Wash  
4.1 Wash with PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 (3 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per change)  

6 Delipidation  
6.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per change)  

7 Rehydration (for refractive index matching)  
7.1 Incubation with 100% hexane (2 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per change)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE; store at RT in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term storage <1 week)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP/YFP in sparse-labeled neurons) while enabling high-resolution visualization of dendritic spines and full dendritic arborization. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method established for ≤500 μm brain slices, compatible with endogenous GFP fluorescence, supports deep antibody penetration, causes minimal morphological distortion, and completes within 1 day. MAP2 is a well-validated dendritic cytoskeletal marker that labels the entire dendritic tree (including fine branches) without labeling axons, making it ideal for spine density normalization against dendritic length. Alexa Fluor 568 is spectrally separable from GFP and fully compatible with MACS, enabling dual-channel imaging of spines (GFP+) and dendritic backbone (MAP2+).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (perform before clearing)  
1.1 Wash fixed 500 μm mouse brain slices 3 × 30 min in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for permeabilization and blocking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody anti-MAP2 (1:500 in blocking solution).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)  
1.4 Wash 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:800 in blocking solution).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours, protected from light)  
1.6 Wash 3 × 1 hour in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Transfer slices to final RI-matching solution: MACS-R2 (same as 2.3) for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes before imaging)  
3.2 Mount cleared slices in glass-bottom dishes or chambered coverslips using MACS-R2 as immersion medium, avoiding bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FOCM  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires rapid (<1 day) transparentization of 500 μm fixed mouse brain slices while preserving endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP/YFP from sparse neuronal labeling) and enabling high-resolution visualization of dendritic spines. FOCM is an aqueous, fast, low-toxicity clearing method specifically validated for thin brain slices (≤500 μm), with excellent preservation of endogenous GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence and minimal tissue distortion—critical for accurate spine density quantification. Although MAP2 is a pan-dendritic marker and not subtype-specific, it is explicitly listed among the acceptable marker candidates for "CA1 树突/树突棘结构辅助" as a structural auxiliary label to support dendritic morphology; combined with endogenous GFP labeling of CA1 neurons (which provides target specificity via genetic targeting), this dual-labeling strategy fulfills the requirement. Alexa Fluor 568 is compatible with FOCM and spectrally separable from GFP, enabling dual-channel imaging of dendritic arbor (MAP2-AF568) and spines (GFP). This combination avoids nuclear counterstains or non-specific dyes that could obscure fine spine morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (perform before clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (mouse or rabbit monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 30 minutes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:800 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 minutes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with FOCM  
2.1 Incubation with FOCM Clearing Solution A: 10% (wt/vol) N-acetylcysteine, 20% (wt/vol) fructose, 0.5% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in distilled water (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FOCM Clearing Solution B: 25% (wt/vol) N-acetylcysteine, 40% (wt/vol) fructose, 1% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in distilled water (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 hours)  

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with FOCM RI Matching Solution: 63% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) N-acetylcysteine, 0.5% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in distilled water (final RI ≈ 1.45) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Transfer slice into glass-bottom imaging dish or chambered coverslip filled with FOCM RI Matching Solution for immediate confocal or light-sheet imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: proceed to imaging within 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires robust identification of mature neurons in dense, lipid-rich human cortical tissue (5 mm thick) using two complementary structural markers: NeuN (nuclear marker of post-mitotic neurons) and MAP2 (dendritic cytoskeleton marker). This dual-target strategy enhances cell detection reliability by co-localizing nuclear and somatodendritic signals. uDISCO is selected because it provides high clearing power for large, lipid- and myelin-rich human brain samples, enables deep antibody penetration, and is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 647—both stable under uDISCO’s organic solvent conditions. Although uDISCO causes some tissue shrinkage, it preserves sufficient 3D architecture for quantitative spatial analysis of neuronal density across cortical layers and perilesional zones. Endogenous fluorescence is not relied upon, so quenching is not a concern.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented clinical samples)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Rehydration: sequential incubation in 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
3.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (3% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total, 4 hours per change)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Post-staining Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBST, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total, 4 hours per change)  

7 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butanol (TBA).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) TBA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.4 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for imaging within 1 month)  
10.2 Mount in DBE-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional RI adjustment.

**Chosen Method:** FOCM  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (endogenous), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FOCM is an aqueous, fast, and low-toxicity clearing method specifically validated for ≤500 μm brain slices, preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., EGFP) and fine dendritic spine morphology with minimal distortion. It enables same-day processing (<8 hours total) while maintaining high signal fidelity—critical for spine density quantification. The dual-labeling strategy uses endogenous EGFP to label spines (e.g., in Thy1-EGFP-M mice) and immunostaining against MAP2 (a dendritic shaft marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 to delineate dendritic arbor geometry, enabling accurate spine counting per unit dendrite length. Both fluorophores are fully compatible with FOCM, and MAP2 staining provides the necessary structural reference without nuclear counterstains that could obscure spine resolution.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (if not pre-labeled)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody anti-MAP2 (1:500 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 30 min) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:800 in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
1.5 Washing with PBS (3 × 20 min) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with FOCM  
2.1 Incubation with FOCM-A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FOCM-B (43% (wt/vol) fructose, 15% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FOCM-C (63% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Transfer slices into imaging chamber filled with FOCM-C (same as step 2.3) for immediate imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥15 min equilibration before acquisition)  
3.2 Seal sample chamber with coverslip using vacuum grease to prevent evaporation during imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源) + MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The original TDE protocol failed due to excessive concentration (100% directly), lack of gradual RI matching, and methanol-based fixation that likely compromised membrane integrity and spine morphology. For rapid (<1 day), high-fidelity clearing of 500 μm brain slices with endogenous FP preservation and reliable dendritic spine visualization, an aqueous, non-denaturing method is essential. MACS is established for thin brain slices (≤500 μm), preserves GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence, enables deep antibody penetration, minimizes tissue shrinkage, and completes within 8–12 hours. MAP2 is a well-validated structural marker for dendritic shafts and branches in CA1 pyramidal neurons, complementing sparse endogenous GFP labeling to enable full dendritic skeleton reconstruction for spine density normalization. Alexa Fluor 647 is compatible with MACS and provides far-red signal with minimal crosstalk and high photostability for high-resolution confocal or light-sheet imaging of spines.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS to reverse methanol-induced artifacts and stabilize cytoarchitecture.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or mouse monoclonal, 1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
3.3 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: anti-host IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) in blocking solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
3.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

4 Dehydration (Optional but recommended for faster clearing kinetics in MACS)  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Tissue Optical Clearing with MACS  
5.1 Incubation with MACS-R0: 20% (vol/vol) N-methyl-D-glucamine (MXDA), 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with MACS-R1: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with MACS-R2: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
6.1 Equilibration in final imaging medium: MACS-R2 (same as 5.3) for optimal RI matching (~1.51).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Mount sample in glass-bottom dish or chambered coverslip filled with fresh MACS-R2, sealed with vacuum grease to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)  

*Note: Total protocol time ≈ 12–14 hours, compatible with same-day processing. Avoid prolonged storage in methanol; all steps post-fixation should be aqueous-based to preserve spine ultrastructure.*

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for small whole embryonic samples (T03 tier), offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology with minimal shrinkage—critical for accurate 3D reconstruction of delicate early neural projections. It supports deep penetration of antibodies and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes and endogenous fluorophores. The dual-labeling strategy targets both pan-neuronal processes (via β-III Tubulin/TUJ1, a well-validated marker for immature and mature neuronal axons in E12.5 embryos) and neural crest-derived glial/precursor populations that guide cranial and spinal nerve pathfinding (via Sox10). This combination enables simultaneous visualization of axonal trajectories and their associated support cells across the entire embryo, fulfilling the goal of mapping continuous nerve paths and analyzing spatial coverage and branching patterns.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash fixed E12.5 mouse embryo 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Sox10 (1:300) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly: 6 × 2 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in blocking solution, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.6 Wash thoroughly: 6 × 2 hours in PBST, then 2 × 1 hour in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: as specified)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 15% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-A solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-B solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-RI matching solution (88% (wt/vol) iodixanol in distilled water, adjusted to RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Transfer embryo to fresh Ce3D-RI matching solution in imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Store cleared embryo in Ce3D-RI matching solution at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 2 weeks. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: as needed)  
4.2 Mount sample in glass-bottom dish or capillary compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, fully immersed in Ce3D-RI solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for small whole embryos (T03 tier), offering excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-derived fluorescence, minimal tissue distortion, and deep penetration of antibodies—critical for tracing delicate early neural projections across the entire E12.5 embryo. The dual-labeling strategy uses β-III Tubulin (TUJ1), a pan-neuronal marker labeling all axons and neurites, combined with Sox10, a transcription factor specifically expressed in neural crest–derived lineages including cranial and peripheral glia and Schwann cell precursors. This pairing enables reliable discrimination of neuronal processes (TUJ1) from their associated glial scaffolds (Sox10), enhancing confidence in identifying true nerve bundles versus isolated cellular extensions during early pathfinding. Both primary antibodies are compatible with Ce3D’s gentle, non-denaturing conditions, and Alexa Fluor 488/568 fluorophores are fully preserved in Ce3D.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Sox10 (1:300) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: total 48 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568 donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: total 48 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A1 reagent (25% (wt/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (THPED), 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-A2 reagent (50% (wt/vol) THPED, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B reagent (50% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 10% (wt/vol) THPED, 5% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber and incubate in Ce3D-Matching Solution (RI ≈ 1.48; composed of 80% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 10% (wt/vol) THPED, 5% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Store and image in Ce3D-Matching Solution at 4 ℃, protected from light, for up to 4 weeks. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: until imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole embryos (T03 tier), preserves endogenous fluorescence (though not required here), and enables deep antibody penetration—critical for visualizing early axonal projections and peripheral nerve structures via β-III Tubulin/TUJ1, a target-specific marker for embryonic cranial/spinal and peripheral neurons. The original dual-labeling included HuC/D, which is a pan-neuronal somatic marker not specific to the embryonic cranial/spinal and peripheral nerve lineage; thus, it violates the requirement for target-specific labeling. TUJ1 alone is a validated, developmentally appropriate marker for this target. Alexa Fluor 647 is fully compatible with Ce3D and provides strong, stable signal in deep tissue with minimal background when paired with extended cold incubation and thorough washing. This protocol ensures target specificity, compatibility, and optimal penetration while preserving morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Primary Antibody Incubation  
1.1 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) diluted in Ce3D Ab Dilution Buffer (Ce3D-A: 10% DMSO, 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) supplemented with 5% normal goat serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

2 Washing  
2.1 Wash with Ce3D Wash Buffer (Ce3D-W: 10% DMSO, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, 3 changes at 8-hour intervals)  
2.2 Additional wash with Ce3D-W. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, 6 changes every 8 hours)  

3 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (for TUJ1) at 1:300 dilution in Ce3D-A with 5% normal goat serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

4 Post-Labeling Washing  
4.1 Wash with Ce3D-W. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, 3 changes)  
4.2 Extended wash with Ce3D-W to reduce background. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours, 9 changes every 8 hours)  

5 Tissue Clearing (Ce3D Protocol)  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution A (25% (wt/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (THP), 15% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  
5.2 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution B (50% (wt/vol) THP, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with Ce3D-RI Matching Solution (63% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS, final RI ≈ 1.45). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Final Equilibration and Storage  
7.1 Transfer sample to fresh Ce3D-RI Matching Solution in imaging-compatible glass vial. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging; store at 4 ℃ in dark for up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for small whole samples (1–5 mm), including Drosophila heads and brains, offering high clearing power essential for dense, lipid-rich neural tissue while enabling deep antibody penetration. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is not a concern here as labeling relies on target-specific primary antibodies conjugated to compatible synthetic dyes. Bruchpilot (nc82) is the canonical marker for Drosophila presynaptic active zones, and Synapsin specifically labels synaptic vesicle clusters—both are validated target-specific markers for the required structures. Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 568 are fully compatible with uDISCO and avoid fluorophore classes flagged with cautions for these targets. uDISCO’s strong delipidation and refractive index matching (~1.52) support high-resolution 3D imaging of synaptic architecture across entire fly brains with acceptable morphological preservation for circuit-level analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:300) and goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:300) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, dark, gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Gradual methanol series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 100% methanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
2.2 Repeat 100% methanol wash (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Clearing  
3.1 Incubation in dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation in DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation in dibenzyl ether (DBE) (final RI ≈ 1.56) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 hours until transparent)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer cleared sample into glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging; store at RT protected from light for up to 1 week)
