**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Neurofilament + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for whole-mount embryos (~1–5 mm), offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching for deep imaging while preserving exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor dyes. It enables excellent penetration of antibodies into dense embryonic tissue and is compatible with both green (Alexa Fluor 488) and far-red (Alexa Fluor 647) channels—critical for dual-labeling mature nerve bundles (Neurofilament) and early extending neurites (β-III Tubulin/TUJ1). Both β-III Tubulin and Neurofilament are target-specific markers for embryonic cranial/spinal and peripheral nerves, satisfying the labeling requirement without relying on pan-lineage or nuclear counterstains. FDISCO is established for tier T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM, provides faster clearing than aqueous alternatives, and maintains signal integrity for antibody-conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes, facilitating continuous 3D tracing of neural projections from CNS to periphery.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Rehydration: stepwise rehydration through 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (15 min each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes per step)  
2.2 Permeabilization and blocking: incubation with blocking buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal donkey serum in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Neurofilament (clone 2H3 or SMI-312, 1:300) in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 2% normal donkey serum in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Wash with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS), 6 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG1 Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) for TUJ1 and donkey anti-mouse IgG2b Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) for Neurofilament, in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Wash with PBST, 6 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

6 Dehydration (post-staining)  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation  
7.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi) until sample becomes transparent.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi) for long-term storage at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
9.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional washing.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method established for small whole samples (1–5 mm) like intact Drosophila heads. It provides strong clearing power necessary for dense, pigment- and lipid-rich tissue while enabling deep antibody penetration—critical for labeling presynaptic active zones and synaptic vesicle regions. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is not a concern here as labeling relies on target-specific immunostaining with Alexa Fluor dyes, which are fully compatible with uDISCO. Bruchpilot (nc82) is a validated marker for the presynaptic active zone, and Synapsin specifically labels synaptic vesicle clusters in Drosophila; both are target-appropriate and paired with fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568) confirmed compatible with uDISCO. The method’s speed and optical clarity support high-resolution 3D imaging of synaptic architecture with minimal compromise to morphology when protocols are carefully followed.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Primary Antibody Incubation  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, dark, gentle agitation)  

4 Post-Labeling Wash  
4.1 Wash with PBST: 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
4.2 Final wash with PBS: 2 changes, 30 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

5 Dehydration (uDISCO)  
5.1 30% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 50% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 70% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Delipidation  
6.1 Incubation in 66% dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation in 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Repeat 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation in 100% ethyl cinnamate (ECi) (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging; store in ECi at RT in the dark)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Store samples in ethyl cinnamate at RT in the dark until imaging (stable for ≥2 weeks)  
8.2 Mount samples in glass-bottom imaging chambers using ethyl cinnamate without air bubbles (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** MACS is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for tier T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM, offering deep antibody penetration and strong clearing power suitable for dense, pigment-rich Drosophila heads while preserving endogenous fluorescence and minimizing tissue shrinkage or distortion—critical for accurate synaptic geometry. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), MACS avoids hazardous reagents and maintains sample integrity. The selected markers—Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) for the presynaptic active zone and Synapsin for synaptic vesicle clusters—are target-specific, well-validated antibodies in Drosophila neuroscience. Both are paired with Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 568, fluorophores fully compatible with MACS and not subject to quenching or cautionary restrictions for these targets. This approach ensures specific synaptic labeling without reliance on nuclear counterstains or non-target structural markers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration and Cuticle Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with PBS + 2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Blocking and Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (PBS + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:300) and goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:300) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, with gentle agitation)  

5 Post-staining Washes  
5.1 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)  

6 Tissue Clearing with MACS  
6.1 Incubation with MACS Solution A (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with MACS Solution B (35% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 35% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with MACS Solution C (45% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 45% (wt/vol) urea, 25% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
7.1 Incubation with MACS Mounting Medium (RI ≈ 1.46, composed of 60% (wt/vol) iodixanol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with fresh MACS Mounting Medium for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (store at 4 ℃ if imaging delayed beyond 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM (intact Drosophila heads/brains) and provides the strong clearing power required for dense, lipid-rich neural tissue while enabling deep antibody penetration. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is not a concern here as labeling relies on target-specific immunostaining with Alexa Fluor–conjugated secondaries, which are fully compatible with uDISCO. Bruchpilot (nc82) is a canonical marker for Drosophila presynaptic active zones, and Synapsin specifically labels synaptic vesicle clusters—both are target-appropriate and not pan-lineage or nuclear counterstains. uDISCO’s high refractive index (~1.52) and rapid clearing kinetics suit the sample size, and morphological preservation is sufficient when protocols are carefully followed, meeting the requirement for minimal distortion in 3D synaptic architecture analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Wash samples 3 × 30 min in PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 (PBT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  
1.2 Block in blocking buffer (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 5% normal goat serum) for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibodies: mouse anti-nc82 (1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash 5 × 1 hour in PBT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:300) and goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:300) in blocking buffer, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.6 Wash 5 × 1 hour in PBT, then 2 × 30 min in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: as indicated)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Dehydrate through an ascending methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%, 100% MeOH in distilled water (v/v), 1 hour each at RT. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  

3 Delipidation and Clearing  
3.1 Incubate in dichloromethane (DCM) for 30 min. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Transfer to fresh DCM for another 30 min. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubate in 100% hexane for 20 min. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)  
3.4 Repeat hexane incubation for 20 min. (Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Incubate in BABB (1:2 benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate) until optically clear (typically 30–60 min). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30–60 minutes)  
4.2 Transfer cleared sample into a glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh BABB. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use)  
4.3 Equilibrate for at least 30 min before imaging to ensure RI homogeneity (RI ≈ 1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Storage (if not imaged immediately)  
5.1 Store samples immersed in BABB at RT in the dark in sealed containers. (Temperature: RT, Time: up to 1 week without significant signal loss; longer storage may increase brittleness)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for hard mineralized tissues like P7 mouse calvaria, offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for deep imaging of dense bone. It enables excellent antibody penetration into thick (~2 mm) cranial samples while preserving fine cellular morphology with minimal distortion compared to other organic solvent methods. Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes. The dual-target strategy uses Osx (Osterix), a transcription factor marking early osteoprogenitors in the suture mesenchyme and osteogenic fronts, and Osteocalcin, a late-stage osteoblast marker enriched in mineralizing bone matrix—enabling spatial discrimination of differentiation stages across suture zones. Nuclear counterstains such as TO-PRO-3 are incompatible with Osteocalcin and Osx per marker-level cautions and have been removed; cellular context will be inferred from target-specific signal morphology and spatial distribution.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, for endogenous pigment/autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Osx (Osterix) rabbit polyclonal antibody (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin goat polyclonal antibody (1:200) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NGS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes).  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NGS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh BABB (1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish filled with BABB (1:2 vol/vol) for immediate light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: as needed for imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically validated for hard mineralized tissues like P7 mouse calvaria, offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for dense bone. It enables deep antibody penetration while effectively suppressing bone autofluorescence—critical for distinguishing true signal from background in the suture microenvironment. Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses target-specific primary antibodies against Osx (marking early osteoprogenitors/pre-osteoblasts) and Osteocalcin (marking mature osteoblasts), each conjugated to spectrally distinct, FDISCO-compatible Alexa Fluor dyes (488 and 647). This dual-marker approach aligns with the scientific goal of spatially resolving differentiation stages across suture zones, while avoiding nuclear counterstains (e.g., DAPI) that exacerbate autofluorescence interference in mineralized tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS), 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBST, 6 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration (reverse methanol series)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Organic Solvent Transition  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in FDISCO, so we use immunolabeling with Alexa Fluor dyes—compatible per the knowledge base. Osx (Osterix) marks early osteoprogenitors/pre-osteoblasts, and Osteocalcin labels mature osteoblasts/osteocytes—both are target-specific markers for 成骨细胞 as required. Lectin was removed because it is not a target-specific marker for 成骨细胞 and is explicitly cautioned against when used with Osteocalcin and Osx per marker-level cautions. **Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like intact mouse bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep antibody penetration into the mineralized femur and efficiently clears lipids and pigments that obstruct imaging in bone marrow. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses robust immunofluorescence with Alexa Fluor dyes—compatible with FDISCO—and targets two key structures: tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) to label sympathetic nerve fibers (a specific marker for bone marrow sympathetic innervation) and CD31 (PECAM1) to visualize vascular endothelium. This dual-channel labeling allows precise 3D mapping of neuro-vascular spatial relationships within the hematopoietic stem cell niche. FDISCO’s relatively fast protocol (days vs. weeks) and compatibility with Alexa Fluor 488/647 make it optimal for this application.

**Protocol Steps:**

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem involves intact mouse femur (hard mineralized tissue) requiring preservation of bone marrow cavity architecture and dual labeling of sympathetic nerve fibers (best marked by tyrosine hydroxylase, TH) and vascular/endothelial structures (best marked by CD31/PECAM1). BoneClear caused excessive brittleness due to harsh organic solvents and rapid dehydration. Ce3D is an aqueous-based, high-penetration clearing method specifically validated for dense tissues like bone and lymphoid organs, with minimal shrinkage/distortion and excellent preservation of antibody-based fluorescence. It avoids the extreme dehydration steps of solvent-based protocols (e.g., BoneClear, FDISCO), thereby reducing mechanical fragility. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are fully compatible with Ce3D and provide bright, photostable signals for deep imaging of TH⁺ sympathetic fibers and CD31⁺ vasculature across marrow zones (central, endosteal, metaphyseal).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution A (25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution B (50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-Mounting Solution (80% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to fresh Ce3D-Mounting Solution in glass-bottom imaging chamber or matched RI cuvette (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging)  
3.2 Store long-term at 4 ℃ in Ce3D-Mounting Solution protected from light (stable for ≥1 month)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically established for dense hard tissues like intact mouse femur, enabling deep antibody penetration into the mineralized bone and marrow cavity. It preserves synthetic fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor dyes) while quenching endogenous fluorescent proteins—thus requiring immunolabeling rather than relying on transgenic reporters. Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers in the bone marrow, and CD31 (PECAM1) robustly labels vascular endothelial cells, allowing precise mapping of neuro-vascular spatial relationships. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are both highly compatible with FDISCO, exhibit strong signal retention after dehydration and delipidation, and enable dual-channel 3D imaging with minimal crosstalk.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (performed prior to clearing; assume fixed femurs are stored in PBS at 4 ℃)  
1.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
1.4 Washing with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (3 changes, 12 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours total)  
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:300) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.6 Washing with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (3 changes, 12 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration (optional intermediate step for FDISCO to stabilize fluorescence)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Dehydration (second round, pre-clearing)  
5.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.5 Final incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer cleared femur into glass vial filled with fresh DBE and seal with parafilm. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage up to 1 week)  
7.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647, Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The mouse cochlea is a dense, mineralized hard tissue embedded in the otic capsule, requiring a high-clearing-power method with deep dye/antibody penetration. FDISCO—a solvent-based, fluorescence-preserving variant of DISCO—is established for hard tissues like bone and cochlea, provides strong delipidation and refractive index homogenization, and is compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles of both inner and outer hair cells with high specificity and signal-to-noise, enabling precise identification of hair cell morphology and loss patterns without antibody amplification. Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, hair cell–specific cytoplasmic marker; labeling with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated antibody ensures robust identification of all hair cell bodies across the entire cochlear spiral. This dual-labeling strategy allows unambiguous discrimination of intact vs. missing hair cells and preserves spatial continuity for 3D reconstruction and automated counting. FDISCO’s organic solvents effectively clear the bony cochlear capsule while maintaining structural integrity better than uDISCO or iDISCO+ for this small but dense organ.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Decalcification (integrated in FDISCO-compatible reagent)  
2.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Immunolabeling and Phalloidin Staining (performed after partial dehydration to enhance penetration)  
3.1 Rehydration: sequential incubation in 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
3.2 Permeabilization and blocking: incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
3.3 Primary antibody incubation: anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.4 Washing: 5 × 1 hour in PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
3.5 Secondary antibody + Phalloidin co-staining: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) + Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.6 Final washing: 3 × 2 hours in PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

4 Re-dehydration (post-labeling)  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Bleaching (optional but recommended for endogenous pigment reduction)  
5.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 ratio).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with BABB for long-term storage at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)  
7.2 Mount in BABB-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional steps.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like intact mouse femur, enabling deep antibody penetration into the bone marrow cavity while preserving fine neural and vascular structures. It efficiently removes lipids and decalcifies minimally fixed mineralized tissue, achieving high transparency with relatively low morphological distortion compared to other solvent methods. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our targets—sympathetic nerve fibers (marked by tyrosine hydroxylase, TH) and vascular endothelium (marked by CD31/PECAM1)—are robustly labeled via immunostaining with bright, photostable Alexa Fluor dyes compatible with FDISCO. Alexa Fluor 568 and 647 exhibit excellent signal retention in FDISCO and allow spectral separation for dual-channel 3D imaging of neuro-vascular spatial relationships in the hematopoietic stem cell niche.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) and donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) diluted in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-Staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
8.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
8.3 Incubation with PBS only.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)  

9 Dehydration (Post-Labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (fresh batch).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (dibenzyl ether, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for final RI matching (RI ≈ 1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

11 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE and seal with parafilm.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite storage, protected from light)  
11.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D acquisition of TH⁺ sympathetic fibers and CD31⁺ vascular networks across central marrow, endosteal, and metaphyseal regions.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method established for dense hard tissues like the bony cochlea (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep penetration of fluorescent dyes and antibodies into mineralized bone-encased spiral structures while preserving fine F-actin architecture. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses direct chemical probes: Phalloidin (which directly binds F-actin in stereocilia bundles without requiring antibodies) and an anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, specific marker for cochlear hair cells). TO-PRO-3 was removed because nuclear counterstains such as TO-PRO-3 (a Hoechst/DAPI analog) are explicitly cautioned against for Myosin VIIa labeling per compatibility guidelines. This revised combination allows simultaneous visualization of hair cell identity (Myosin VIIa) and apical actin cytoskeleton (Phalloidin), fulfilling all scientific goals including damage assessment across cochlear turns without violating fluorophore-marker compatibility constraints.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4, with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

2 Immunolabeling and Phalloidin Staining  
2.1 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibody: rabbit anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200) + Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  
2.4 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 4 changes, gentle shaking)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

4 Delipidation and Bleaching  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
4.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh 100% ECi and seal with parafilm.(Temperature: RT, protected from light, indefinite storage)  
6.2 Mount in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI ≈ 1.56).

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense mineralized tissues like the otic capsule surrounding the mouse cochlea. It enables deep penetration of antibodies and small-molecule dyes while achieving strong transparency in hard tissues—addressing the user’s failure with BoneClear (insufficient decalcification/decoloration and poor signal). Myosin VIIa is a well-established, specific marker for both inner and outer hair cells in the cochlea, allowing accurate identification and counting. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles without requiring genetic reporters or additional antibodies, preserving fine structural detail critical for assessing noise-induced damage. Both Alexa Fluor 647 and 488 are fully compatible with FDISCO and provide bright, photostable signals with low background in deep tissue. This combination fulfills all scientific goals: cell identity, stereocilia integrity, regional damage mapping, and 3D reconstruction in intact cochleae.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling and Cytoskeletal Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody against Myosin VIIa (1:200 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300 in blocking solution) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated Phalloidin (1:100) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Decolorization and Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide in 100% methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of DCM and dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with fresh 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE and seal (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
5.2 Mount in DBE-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The mouse cochlea is a dense, mineralized hard tissue embedded in the otic capsule, requiring a high-clearing-power method with deep dye/antibody penetration. FDISCO—a solvent-based, FP-quenching but dye-compatible protocol—is established for hard tissues like bone and cochlea, offering rapid, strong delipidation and refractive index (RI) matching suitable for light-sheet or confocal imaging of intact spiral structures. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin–rich stereocilia bundles without antibodies, enabling high-resolution visualization of bundle integrity; Myosin VIIa is a specific marker for cochlear hair cells, allowing precise identification and quantification along the tonotopic axis. TO-PRO-3 was removed as nuclear counterstains (including TO-PRO-3) are not target-specific and are cautioned against for Myosin VIIa labeling per domain guidance. This combination enables automated 3D mapping of hair cell loss and stereocilia disruption across cochlear regions while adhering to labeling specificity and compatibility constraints.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared from 30% H₂O₂: 1 vol H₂O₂ + 5 vol MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  

5 Immunolabeling and Phalloidin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibody anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS) + Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.2 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)  
5.3 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:300 in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.4 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)  

6 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage)  
8.2 Mount in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, TH + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires distinguishing pan-neuronal (泛神经) fibers from sympathetic-specific fibers within the dense, mineralized environment of intact mouse molars. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) and tyrosine hydroxylase (TH, a specific marker for sympathetic neurons) are well-established target-specific markers for this purpose. Although PGP9.5 is pan-neuronal, it is explicitly listed as a valid target-specific marker for 牙髓神经 in the knowledge base and is appropriate when used in combination with a subtype-specific marker like TH to resolve neural subpopulations. Since endogenous fluorescent proteins are not mentioned and hard tissues like teeth lack reliable FP expression, antibody-based labeling with bright, photostable Alexa Fluor dyes is optimal. FDISCO is selected because it is an established solvent-based clearing method for hard tissues (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA tier), provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration into mineralized matrices, preserves Alexa Fluor fluorescence efficiently, and achieves high transparency in small (~2 mm) samples within days. Although FDISCO uses hazardous solvents, its speed and compatibility with the chosen dyes make it ideal for this application.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for hard tissue autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for antibody labeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-PGP9.5 (1:200) and anti-TH (1:200) diluted in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 2% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 2% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Post-labeling Washing  
8.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh BABB for long-term storage at 4 ℃ in the dark.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite until imaging)  
12.2 Mount sample in BABB-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional steps.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for hard tissues like teeth (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for dense mineralized samples while preserving 3D architecture with minimal distortion. It supports deep penetration of lipophilic tracers (e.g., DiI) and antibody-conjugated dyes. Since the goal is to trace the full trajectory of pulp nerve fibers—not subtype identity—a combination of DiI (which labels neuronal membranes via diffusion along axons from root apex) and pan-neuronal marker PGP9.5 (a well-validated target-specific marker for dental pulp nerves) provides complementary, robust labeling without requiring transgenic models. FDISCO quenches endogenous FPs but is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes and DiI, making this dual-labeling strategy optimal for complete nerve path visualization.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-clearing Wash  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Neuronal Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate (DiI) at 5 µg/mL in 100% ethanol, applied directly to root apex region under stereomicroscope using fine glass needle; incubate covered in dark.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
2.2 Post-DiI wash with PBST to remove unbound dye.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.3 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with primary antibody against PGP9.5 (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
2.6 Washing with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  
2.7 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated secondary antibody (1:400 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
2.8 Final wash with PBST until background fluorescence is minimal.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.6 Repeat 100% methanol change.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Delipidation and Bleaching  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 vol 30% H₂O₂ with 5 vol methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

5 Rehydration (reverse methanol series)  
5.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Organic Solvent Transition  
6.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Repeat 100% DCM change.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Final incubation in fresh 100% DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until sample is optically transparent and ready for imaging)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Store cleared tooth in sealed glass vial filled with DBE at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite short-term storage)  
8.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles around the tooth.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method with high clearing power suitable for dense, mineralized hard tissues like intact mouse molars (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep antibody and dye penetration while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes such as Alexa Fluor conjugates. PGP9.5 (protein gene product 9.5) is a pan-neuronal marker highly specific for dental pulp nerves, ideal for visualizing the 3D architecture of nerve fibers in pulp horns, central pulp, and apical regions. Phalloidin labels F-actin in soft tissue cytoskeleton, delineating pulp tissue boundaries and structural integrity without requiring genetic reporters. Both labels are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent environment and provide complementary contrast for neural and stromal compartments.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching (optional but recommended for hard tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-PGP9.5 primary antibody (1:200 dilution in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% normal goat serum) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated Phalloidin (1:100 dilution).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining (if needed; skip if directly conjugated primary used)  
*Note: In this protocol, PGP9.5 is detected using an unconjugated primary antibody followed by a directly conjugated secondary antibody.*  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse or anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, RI ≈ 1.557).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample into a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)  
11.2 Store at RT in sealed container with ECi for up to 1 week if not imaged immediately.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, DiI]  
**Justification:** The sample consists of dense hard-soft tissue composites (vertebrae, paravertebral muscle, peripheral nerves) requiring strong delipidation and high refractive index matching for deep imaging of fine peripheral nerves. FDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA, offering rapid, high-clearing power with excellent dye penetration and compatibility with lipophilic tracers (DiI) and antibody-conjugated fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 647). Although PGP9.5 is a pan-neuronal marker, it is explicitly listed as a valid target-specific marker candidate for both “骨组织感觉神经与泛神经网络” and “运动神经末梢/轴突骨架” in the provided context, satisfying the requirement for target-specific labeling. FDISCO quenches endogenous FPs, but this is irrelevant as no FP expression is assumed; both Alexa Fluor 647 and DiI are fully compatible with FDISCO chemistry, and PGP9.5 is not among the markers flagged for avoidance with DAPI/Hoechst or PI/Draq5—note that no such nuclear counterstains are used here.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-Clearing Staining (Combined Immunolabeling & Lipophilic Tracer)  
1.1 Incubation with primary antibody: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500 in PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 5% DMSO + 0.02% NaN₃) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
1.2 Wash with PBST (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  
1.3 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300 in PBST + 5% DMSO + 0.02% NaN₃) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.4 Concurrently, microinjection of DiI (2 mg/mL in DMSO) into proximal nerve roots under stereomicroscope using glass micropipette (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes injection + immediate transfer to labeling buffer)  
1.5 Post-labeling wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 2 changes)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 changes)  

4 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing counterstain; skip if not needed)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Organic Solvent Transition  
5.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) methanol:dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 changes)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Final incubation in fresh 100% DBE for imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour until imaging)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Store sample immersed in DBE in glass vial wrapped in aluminum foil at RT (stable for weeks)  
7.2 Mount in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy (no additional mounting medium required)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, SV2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The sample consists of dense hard tissue (vertebrae with bone, cartilage) and surrounding muscle containing both general peripheral nerve fibers and motor nerve terminals at neuromuscular junctions. FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method established for T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA, enabling deep penetration into mineralized and lipid-rich tissues while preserving dye-based fluorescence. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in FDISCO, so antibody-based labeling is required. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) labels the entire peripheral nerve network, fulfilling the requirement for visualizing 骨组织感觉神经与泛神经网络. SV2 (synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2) is a target-specific marker for 运动神经末梢/轴突骨架 at neuromuscular junctions, replacing the non-target-specific MBP (which labels myelin but not motor nerve terminals directly). Alexa Fluor 647 and 488 are compatible with FDISCO and provide spectrally distinct, photostable signals for 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-SV2 (1:200) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing PBT every 1–2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: total 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, changing PBT every 1–2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: total 12 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi for final RI matching (RI ≈ 1.558).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

11 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi and seal tightly.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
11.2 Mount sample in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, MBP + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The sample consists of dense hard tissue (vertebrae with bone, cartilage) and surrounding muscle containing both general peripheral nerve fibers and myelinated subsets. FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method established for T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA, enabling deep penetration into mineralized and lipid-rich tissues while preserving dye-based fluorescence. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in FDISCO, so antibody-based labeling is required. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) labels the entire peripheral nerve network, while MBP (myelin basic protein) specifically highlights thick, myelinated fibers—fulfilling the dual goal of visualizing overall architecture and myelinated subpopulations. Alexa Fluor 647 and 488 are compatible with FDISCO and provide spectrally distinct, photostable signals for 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-MBP (1:200) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing PBT every 1–2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: total 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, changing PBT every 1–2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: total 12 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi for final RI matching (RI ≈ 1.558).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

11 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi and seal tightly.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
11.2 Mount sample in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)
