**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem requires preservation of endogenous mCherry/RFP fluorescence in a whole adult mouse for single-cell-resolution detection of disseminated breast cancer micrometastases. Among established whole-body clearing methods, MACS is aqueous-based, non-denaturing, and explicitly compatible with RFP/mCherry signals—unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) that quench or degrade fluorescent proteins. Additionally, while mCherry provides tumor cell localization, it may suffer from tissue autofluorescence or false-positive granular signals; thus, we complement it with immunostaining against Pan-Cytokeratin (a pan-epithelial marker highly specific for carcinoma cells of breast origin) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, which is compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from mCherry. This dual-labeling strategy enhances specificity for true epithelial tumor cells while retaining endogenous signal for rapid screening. MACS also enables deep antibody penetration in whole-body samples and avoids hazardous solvents, making it ideal for high-fidelity, whole-organism 3D mapping of micrometastases.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with MACS-P1 (5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with fresh MACS-P1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling for Pan-Cytokeratin  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (MACS-B: 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (e.g., clone AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution) in MACS-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  
2.3 Wash with MACS-W (5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Repeat wash with MACS-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution) in MACS-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  
2.6 Wash with MACS-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.7 Repeat wash with MACS-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20% (vol/vol) MXDA, 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
4.1 Transfer sample to final imaging medium: MACS-R2 (same as 3.3) in glass container (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage at RT, protected from light)  
4.2 Equilibrate for at least 24 hours before light-sheet or confocal imaging to ensure uniform RI matching and minimize spherical aberration.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous mCherry/RFP fluorescence from tumor cells across the entire adult mouse body, including dense organs and bone marrow niches. Among established whole-body clearing methods, MACS is aqueous-based, non-denaturing, and explicitly compatible with red fluorescent proteins (including mCherry/RFP), unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) that quench or destabilize FPs. MACS also enables deep penetration of antibodies for validation labeling. To confirm tumor identity and exclude false positives from autofluorescence or non-epithelial debris, we add immunostaining for Pan-Cytokeratin—a pan-epithelial marker highly specific for carcinomas—including breast cancer metastases. Alexa Fluor 647 is chosen as the secondary fluorophore due to its photostability, far-red emission (minimizing spectral overlap with mCherry), and compatibility with MACS. This dual-signal strategy (mCherry + Pan-CK) ensures high-confidence identification of micro-metastases at single-cell resolution in lung, liver, brain, bone, and lymph nodes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with anti-Pan-Cytokeratin primary antibody (e.g., mouse monoclonal AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution) in antibody dilution buffer (1% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Wash with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 6 buffer changes every 4 hours)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300 dilution) in antibody dilution buffer (1% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Wash with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, with 8 buffer changes every 6 hours, protected from light)  

6 Tissue Optical Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
7.1 Incubation with final RI matching solution: MACS-R3 (60 vol% MXDA, 60% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.52) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Store sample in MACS-R3 at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging. For light-sheet microscopy, mount in a glass capillary or chamber filled with MACS-R3.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous mCherry/RFP fluorescence in a whole adult mouse for systemic micro-metastasis screening, combined with epithelial tumor cell validation via immunostaining. Among established whole-body clearing methods, MACS is aqueous-based, preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including mCherry/RFP), enables deep antibody penetration, and minimizes tissue distortion—critical for accurate 3D quantification of single-cell metastases. Pan-Cytokeratin is a well-validated pan-epithelial marker that specifically labels carcinoma cells (including breast cancer) and is compatible with MACS when paired with Alexa Fluor 647, which exhibits high stability and minimal quenching in this system. This dual-channel strategy (mCherry + Pan-CK-AF647) ensures reliable identification of true micro-metastatic foci while excluding false positives from autofluorescence or non-epithelial cells.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Pan-Cytokeratin primary antibody (e.g., mouse monoclonal AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution in antibody dilution buffer: 3% BSA, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with washing buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat washing buffer incubation (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Repeat washing buffer incubation (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution in antibody dilution buffer) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, gentle agitation)  

6 Post-Staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with washing buffer (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat washing buffer incubation (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Optical Clearing with MACS  
7.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Incubation with final RI matching solution: MACS-R3 (50 vol% MXDA, 60% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.52) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Store sample in MACS-R3 at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging. Compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy using 561 nm (mCherry) and 640 nm (Alexa Fluor 647) excitation.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, SV2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample consists of dense hard tissue (vertebrae with mineralized bone and cartilage) combined with muscle and peripheral nerves—requiring a high-clearing-power method compatible with deep antibody penetration and strong autofluorescence suppression. FDISCO is an established solvent-based protocol for T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA, offering rapid, effective delipidation and decalcification-like clearing without full demineralization, while preserving fine neural morphology. It quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins but is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 488/647 conjugates. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) labels all peripheral nerve fibers, fulfilling the requirement for visualizing 骨组织感觉神经与泛神经网络. However, MBP is not listed among the valid target-specific markers for the required labeling targets; instead, SV2—a validated marker for 运动神经末梢/轴突骨架—is substituted to specifically label presynaptic terminals at neuromuscular junctions, satisfying the dual requirement to visualize both sensory/pan-neural networks in bone and motor nerve terminals in paravertebral muscle. FDISCO includes a critical H₂O₂/methanol step that effectively reduces bone autofluorescence without compromising far-red signals like Alexa Fluor 647.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Autofluorescence Quenching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-SV2 (1:300) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (3% donkey serum, 0.2% Tween-20, 5% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Wash with PBSTw (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS), 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
6.2 Wash with PBSTw + 5% DMSO, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (for PGP9.5) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (for SV2), each at 1:500 in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-Staining Washes  
8.1 Wash with PBSTw + 5% DMSO, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
8.2 Wash with PBSTw, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (Post-Staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Repeat incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Transfer to fresh BABB for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes before imaging)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in BABB in glass vials wrapped in aluminum foil at RT.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite until imaging)  
12.2 Mount sample in BABB-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous mCherry/RFP signal in a whole adult mouse, which rules out solvent-based methods that quench fluorescent proteins (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). CUBIC failed due to insufficient hemoglobin clearance and slow kinetics in dense whole-body samples. MACS is an aqueous, high-refractive-index clearing method established for whole adult mice, compatible with mCherry/RFP and deep antibody penetration. It effectively reduces heme-derived background through its MXDA/sorbitol formulation and supports robust immunolabeling. Pan-Cytokeratin is a well-validated epithelial/tumor cell marker suitable for detecting micrometastases and epithelial cancer cell residues across organs; conjugation to Alexa Fluor 647 ensures spectral separation from mCherry and compatibility with MACS. This dual-channel strategy enables specific identification of target lesions while excluding autofluorescence or residual pigment artifacts.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Pre-Clearing Wash  
1.1 Post-fixation wash with 0.1 M PBS (pH 7.4) containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) DMSO and 5% (vol/vol) glycerol in 0.1 M PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Hemoglobin Clearance and Decolorization  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-Bleach solution (5% (wt/vol) N-Lauroylsarcosine sodium salt, 25% (vol/vol) DMSO, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.05% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in 0.1 M PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (clone AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution) in antibody dilution buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in 0.1 M PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.3 Wash with 0.1 M PBS containing 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300 dilution) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
3.5 Wash with 0.1 M PBS containing 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  

4 Tissue Optical Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20% (vol/vol) MXDA, 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol in 0.1 M PBS, RI ≈ 1.40).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in 0.1 M PBS, RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in 0.1 M PBS, RI ≈ 1.51).(Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
5.1 Final incubation in MACS-R2 for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥24 hours before imaging; store at RT in the dark)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-refractive-index clearing method specifically optimized for lipid- and pigment-rich tissues like melanoma, offering strong delipidation and depigmentation capacity while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes. It effectively reduces light scattering and absorption from melanin, enabling deep imaging of vascular networks in intact ~10 mm tumors. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) binds specifically to glycoproteins on the luminal surface of endothelial cells, providing robust, direct labeling of perfusable microvasculature without requiring antibody penetration—critical in dense, pigmented tumors. Alexa Fluor 647 is highly compatible with FDISCO, exhibits minimal quenching, and offers deep-tissue imaging in the far-red channel with low autofluorescence. This combination avoids reliance on endogenous fluorescent proteins (which are absent here) and bypasses the need for additional endothelial markers like CD31, as lectin alone suffices for complete vascular network visualization per problem constraints.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Depigmentation  
2.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Vascular Labeling (performed prior to dehydration; if not pre-labeled, integrate here via rehydration-relabeling cycle)  
3.1 Rehydrate through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PBS (15 min each, RT).  
3.2 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS for blocking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with Lectin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin, 50 µg/mL) in PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.4 Wash with PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
3.5 Re-dehydrate through ascending methanol series (20% → 100%, 1 hour each step, RT) before proceeding to Step 2.  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) DCM : ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, RI ≈ 1.558).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi) and seal tightly.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite storage)  
5.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional steps.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically optimized for high-pigment, lipid-rich tissues like melanoma, offering strong delipidation and depigmentation power while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes. It is compatible with both Lectin and CD31 immunolabeling, enabling dual-channel discrimination: intravenously perfused Lectin-Alexa Fluor 647 labels only *functional*, perfused vascular lumens at the time of sacrifice, while anti-CD31-Alexa Fluor 488 reveals the *structural* endothelial network regardless of perfusion status. FDISCO’s high refractive index matching (~1.52) enables deep imaging in dense tumor cores, and its organic solvent system effectively reduces melanin-induced light scattering—critical for 8–10 mm pigmented tumors. Endogenous fluorescence is quenched, but this is irrelevant as labeling relies on exogenous dyes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Initial Tissue Handling  
1.1 Intracardiac perfusion of live mouse with ice-cold PBS (10 mL) followed by 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS (20 mL).(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 min perfusion each)  
1.2 Immediately after perfusion, inject 50 µg/mL Lectin (from *Lycopersicon esculentum*, directly conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647) in PBS retro-orbitally or via left ventricle to label functional vasculature; circulate for 2 min before final PFA fixation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 min circulation + 10 min post-fix)  
1.3 Excise tumor with ~2 mm surrounding tissue; post-fix in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
1.4 Wash in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 min)  

2 Immunolabeling for Structural Vasculature  
2.1 Block in PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubate with rat anti-mouse CD31 primary antibody (1:200 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
2.3 Wash thoroughly in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubate with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
2.5 Final wash in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation and Depigmentation  
4.1 Incubation with 1/3 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 2/3 (vol/vol) DCM in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 min)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Transfer to fresh 100% ECi for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount cleared tumor in glass-bottom dish filled with ECi; orient for optimal light-sheet or confocal z-stack acquisition through tumor core and periphery.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically optimized for high-pigment, lipid-rich tissues like melanoma, offering strong delipidation and effective melanin removal while preserving far-red fluorescence. It is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 568 and 647 conjugates and supports deep penetration of lectin and anti-CD31 antibodies. Lectin perfusion labels functional, perfused vascular lumens, while CD31 immunostaining reveals the full structural endothelial network—including non-perfused or collapsed vessels—enabling direct comparison of perfusion status versus structural integrity across tumor regions. The use of red/far-red fluorophores minimizes residual melanin absorption and scattering, maximizing signal-to-noise in deep tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion-Based Vascular Lumen Labeling (pre-clearing)  
1.1 Intracardial perfusion with ice-cold PBS (10 mL) followed by 50 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin in PBS (5 mL) at physiological pressure.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)  
1.2 Post-fixation with 4% PFA in PBS via perfusion (10 mL).(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

2 Tissue Harvest and Post-Fixation  
2.1 Dissect intact melanoma (8–10 mm diameter) and immerse in 4% PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Wash 3× with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Immunostaining for Structural Vasculature  
3.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal goat serum in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1), 1:100 dilution in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [p63 + Alexa Fluor 488, Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires spatial discrimination of basal cell layer (via p63) and luminal/epithelial adenocarcinoma cells (via Pan-Cytokeratin) across the full 15 mm needle core to assess gland architecture, fusion, and Gleason-relevant patterns. MACS is selected because it is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for dense human clinical blocks (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), preserves antibody-based fluorescence (compatible with Alexa Fluor 488/568), enables deep penetration into 15 mm tissue, and minimizes morphological distortion—critical for accurate 3D Gleason pattern reconstruction. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), MACS avoids tissue shrinkage and hazardous reagents while maintaining high transparency in lipid-rich prostate tissue. DAPI was removed from labeling as it is a nuclear counterstain and not a target-specific marker for prostate glandular structures, per protocol requirements.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-p63 (1:200) and rabbit anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Transfer cleared tissue into fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage or immediate imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  
3.2 Mount sample vertically in a glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 to maintain orientation along the 15 mm axis. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to light-sheet or confocal microscopy)

**Justification:** uDISCO is an established high-clearing-power solvent-based method for dense human clinical tissue blocks (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), enabling deep antibody penetration and rapid processing within several days. Pan-Cytokeratin is a validated target-specific marker for epithelial carcinoma cells, and when conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (compatible with uDISCO), provides robust tumor cell labeling. Nuclear counterstains such as TO-PRO-3 are not target-specific and are cautioned against for Pan-Cytokeratin labeling per compatibility guidelines; thus, only the target-specific immunolabel is retained. This labeling strategy meets the requirement of identifying residual epithelial cancer cells in 3D without using non-listed fluorophores, non-target-specific markers, or incompatible stain combinations.

1 Dehydration

1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.3 Rehydration: Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.4 Rehydration: Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.5 Wash: Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 6 buffer changes at 4-hour intervals)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

9 Re-dehydration  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Final RI Matching and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Mount sample in glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ in dark for ≤1 week)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [p63 + Alexa Fluor 647, Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D visualization of prostate gland architecture—specifically distinguishing cancerous from benign glands based on the continuity of the basal cell layer (marked by p63) and the identity of luminal epithelial cells (marked by Pan-Cytokeratin). Both p63 and Pan-Cytokeratin are target-specific markers for prostate gland structures in clinical pathology contexts. iDISCO+ is selected because it provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration in dense human clinical tissue (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), which is critical for 15 mm-long needle cores. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is irrelevant here as labeling relies on immunostaining with compatible Alexa Fluor dyes. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are both compatible with iDISCO+, enabling dual-channel specific labeling. DAPI has been removed due to marker-level cautions against its use with p63 and to adhere strictly to target-specific labeling without non-specific nuclear counterstains. The method’s speed and established use in dense human tissues make it optimal for diagnostic-relevant throughput.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Rehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-p63 (1:200) and anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 10% DMSO + 6% donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Repeat wash step 6.1.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-Staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Repeat DBE incubation in fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [p63 + Alexa Fluor 488, Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for dense human clinical tissues (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK) that preserves tissue morphology with minimal shrinkage—critical for maintaining the 1 mm × 15 mm needle core geometry. It supports deep antibody penetration without aggressive dehydration or rapid RI shifts that cause distortion in FOCM/DBE protocols. p63 specifically labels basal cells of prostate glands, fulfilling the requirement for a target-specific marker for prostate glandular structure; Pan-Cytokeratin robustly marks luminal and cancerous epithelial cells and serves as a complementary structural marker to enable 3D assessment of basal layer integrity, gland fusion, cribriform patterns, and invasive growth. Both primary antibodies are compatible with Ce3D and can be paired with Alexa Fluor 488/568, which are fully compatible per method-fluorophore guidelines. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains alone are not target-specific labeling and are cautioned against when used with p63 per marker-level cautions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in ethanol/methanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.4 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, with 2 buffer changes)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Permeabilization Buffer (0.5% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 0.1 M glycine in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-Blocking Buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-p63 (mouse monoclonal, 1:200) and anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (rabbit polyclonal, 1:300) diluted in Ce3D-Antibody Dilution Buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle agitation)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Wash Buffer (0.5% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 4 buffer changes every 6 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in Ce3D-Antibody Dilution Buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  

6 Post-Staining Wash  
6.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Wash Buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 4 buffer changes)  
6.2 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, 2 changes)  

7 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution A (10% w/v N-methylnicotinamide, 10% w/v urea, 10% w/v sucrose in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution B (25% w/v N-methylnicotinamide, 25% w/v urea, 25% w/v sucrose in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with Ce3D-Mounting Solution (50% w/v N-methylnicotinamide, 50% w/v iodixanol, final RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer tissue to fresh Ce3D-Mounting Solution in glass-bottom imaging chamber (Temperature: 4 ℃, store in dark until imaging)  
8.2 Equilibrate at RT for 1 hour before light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI matched to objective immersion medium)

**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D mapping of high endothelial venules (HEVs) within intact murine inguinal lymph nodes (~2–3 mm), which are dense immune organs with tightly packed lymphocyte zones. HEVs are best identified by the carbohydrate epitope PNAd (recognized by MECA-79 antibody), a specific marker for HEV luminal surfaces, complemented by pan-endothelial CD31 to delineate the full vascular scaffold. MACS is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole immune organs (T03 tier), preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes, enables deep antibody penetration without quenching, and minimizes tissue distortion—critical for spatial analysis of HEV-immune cell topography. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), MACS avoids shrinkage that could misrepresent microanatomical relationships. DAPI was removed as it is not target-specific and is cautioned against when used with CD19 (though not used here, consistency with marker-level cautions and target-specific labeling principles warrants its exclusion).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation; assume samples fixed in 4% PFA, PBS-washed)

1.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Primary antibody incubation: anti-PNAd (MECA-79, rat IgM) at 1:100 and anti-CD31 (rat IgG2a) at 1:100 in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Washing with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.5 Secondary antibody incubation: goat anti-rat IgM-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and goat anti-rat IgG2a-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:200) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [MECA-79 (anti-PNAd) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and high refractive index matching in dense, small whole tissues like lymph nodes (2–3 mm), enabling deep antibody penetration and excellent preservation of fine vascular architecture. It is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes. PNAd is the gold-standard target-specific marker for HEVs in murine lymphoid tissue, recognized by the MECA-79 antibody, and is superior to non-HEV markers such as CD19 or B220 (which label lymphocytes). CD31 (PECAM1) serves as a pan-endothelial reference to contextualize HEV localization within the broader vascular network. Nuclear counterstains such as Hoechst are not target-specific for HEVs and are unnecessary for the primary labeling objective; their inclusion is omitted to adhere strictly to target-specific labeling requirements. FDISCO robustly preserves synthetic fluorophores like Alexa Fluor 488 and 647, which are both compatible with this method.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rat anti-mouse PNAd (MECA-79, BioLegend, 1:100) and rat anti-mouse CD31 (BD Pharmingen, 1:100) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rat IgM Alexa Fluor 647 (for MECA-79) and donkey anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (for CD31), both at 1:200 in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide in 100% methanol (prepared fresh: 1 part 30% H₂O₂ + 5 parts methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in hexane. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich, 112372) for final RI matching (RI ≈ 1.558). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer cleared lymph node into fresh ethyl cinnamate in a glass imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PNAd (MECA-79) + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires specific labeling of high endothelial venules (HEVs), for which PNAd (peripheral node addressin) is the canonical surface marker uniquely expressed on HEVs in lymph nodes. CD31 provides pan-endothelial structural context to delineate the full vascular network. iDISCO+ is selected because it offers strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration in dense, small whole tissues like lymph nodes (~2–3 mm), is established for T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM, and is compatible with Alexa Fluor 568/647 dyes. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous FPs, our labeling relies on robust antibody-conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes, which are fully compatible. Organic solvent-based clearing ensures high transparency and refractive index matching suitable for high-resolution light-sheet or confocal imaging of intact lymph node architecture. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific and are listed with “caution” for iDISCO+; moreover, the requirement specifies that nuclear stains do not substitute for target-specific labeling.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

8 Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT + 0.2% heparin (6 changes over 24 hours).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [MECA-79 (anti-PNAd) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires specific labeling of high endothelial venules (HEVs), which are best identified by the addressin PNAd (recognized by MECA-79 antibody), not by generic B-cell markers like CD19 or B220. CD31 (PECAM1) serves as a pan-vascular endothelial marker to delineate all blood vessels, enabling spatial comparison with HEVs. Nuclear counterstains such as Hoechst are not target-specific and are excluded per labeling requirements. MACS is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole lymph nodes (T03 tier), preserves antigenicity better than harsh organic solvents (e.g., iDISCO+/uDISCO), enables deep antibody penetration, and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes—addressing the user’s issues of weak HEV signal and high background from prior DCM/DBE-based solvent clearing.

1 Antibody Staining (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rat anti-mouse PNAd (MECA-79, 1:100) and rat anti-mouse CD31 (1:100) in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 changes every 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-rat IgM-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and goat anti-rat IgG-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 changes every 2 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

CD31 (PECAM1) serves as a pan-vascular endothelial marker to delineate all blood vessels, enabling spatial comparison with HEVs. Hoechst provides nuclear counterstain for lymphocyte-rich zones without interfering with far-red channels. MACS is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole lymph nodes (T03 tier), preserves antigenicity better than harsh organic solvents (e.g., iDISCO+/uDISCO), enables deep antibody penetration, and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes and Hoechst—addressing the user’s issues of weak HEV signal and high background from prior DCM/DBE-based solvent clearing.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD19+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-resolution 3D mapping of B cell follicles in intact mouse spleen (~15 mm), a dense lymphoid organ with high lipid content. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM samples, offering strong delipidation, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes—critical for robust labeling of B cell-specific markers. Endogenous fluorescence is not relied upon; instead, we use two complementary B cell lineage markers: B220 (pan-B cell marker) and CD19 (mature B cell marker), conjugated to spectrally distinct, iDISCO+-compatible Alexa Fluor dyes (647 and 568). This dual-labeling strategy ensures specific, high-contrast visualization of B cell follicles in white pulp while avoiding non-specific nuclear stains (e.g., DAPI) as primary markers. iDISCO+’s organic solvent workflow efficiently clears large, fixed spleens within days with minimal autofluorescence, enabling light-sheet or confocal imaging of spatial follicle architecture along the splenic long axis and marginal zones.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if tissue pigmentation observed)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-mouse B220 (PTPRC) (1:200) and rat anti-mouse CD19 (1:200) in PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 three times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)

7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 647, PNA-Lectin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for dense mouse soft organs (5–20 mm), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody/lectin penetration—critical for visualizing B cell follicles and germinal centers throughout the intact spleen. It preserves morphology with acceptable shrinkage and is fully compatible with both Alexa Fluor dyes and lectins. B220 (PTPRC) robustly labels all B cells, defining follicular architecture; PNA-Lectin specifically binds to germinal center B cells, enabling direct identification of vaccine-induced GCs without requiring additional markers like GL7 (not in allowed list). DAPI is omitted due to compatibility cautions with lectin-based labeling and target-specificity requirements; nuclear context is inferred from cellular morphology and dense B220/PNA signal patterns. Endogenous FPs are avoided per solvent-method limitations; all labeling uses exogenous, compatible fluorophores.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented tissue; include for spleen due to heme content)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary and Secondary Labeling (combined direct labeling strategy)  
5.1 Incubation with labeling solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin + rat anti-mouse B220 (PTPRC) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) + biotinylated PNA-Lectin (1:200).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
5.2 Wash with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 6 changes every 4 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) in PBST + 5% DMSO + 0.2% heparin to amplify PNA signal.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.4 Final wash with PBST + 5% DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 6 changes)  

6 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation  
7.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in amber glass vial until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
9.2 Mount in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, avoiding bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3 + Alexa Fluor 488, CD8 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep, high-fidelity 3D mapping of total T cells (via CD3) and cytotoxic T cells (via CD8) in a dense, fixed ~8 mm mouse subcutaneous tumor. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for this tissue tier (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM), offering strong delipidation power for dense tumors, excellent antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor 488/647—critical for distinguishing two T cell populations simultaneously. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous FPs, our labeling relies on exogenous antibody-conjugated Alexa dyes, which are fully compatible. DAPI was removed from the labeling scheme because it is not a target-specific marker for tumor-infiltrating T cells and is listed with "caution" for use with CD3/CD8 under iDISCO+, potentially compromising signal reliability and violating target-specificity requirements.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for pigmented tumors)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-mouse CD3ε (clone 17A2) at 1:200 and rat anti-mouse CD8α (clone 53-6.7) at 1:200 in PBT + 5% donkey serum + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 five more times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (for CD3) and donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (for CD8), each at 1:500 in PBT + 5% donkey serum + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 five more times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Final RI Matching and Storage  
12.1 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging; samples can be stored at RT in DBE for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 647, GL7+Alexa Fluor 568, PNA-Lectin+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The spleen is a highly pigmented, lipid-rich organ (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH), requiring a high-clearing-power solvent-based method. FDISCO provides strong delipidation and efficient hemoglobin decolorization while preserving fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes and lectins—unlike iDISCO+, which shows caution for PNA-Lectin and potential incompatibility with certain labeling strategies. FDISCO supports deep antibody penetration and is fully compatible with all chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568/647 and PNA-Lectin), enabling robust multichannel 3D imaging of B cell follicles and germinal centers. B220 labels all B cells to delineate follicles; GL7 marks activated B cells in germinal centers; PNA-Lectin specifically binds germinal center extracellular matrix, enabling precise identification of GCs. Endogenous fluorescence is avoided due to quenching by solvent-based methods, so all labeling uses exogenous Alexa-conjugated reagents. The protocol includes extended H₂O₂/methanol decolorization and gradient dehydration/delipidation to eliminate residual heme pigment and ensure uniform clearing with minimal distortion.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Decolorization  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-B220 (1:200) and rat anti-GL7 (1:100) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300), donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 568 (1:300), and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated PNA-Lectin (10 µg/mL) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 647, GL7+Alexa Fluor 568, CD35/CD21 (for follicular dendritic cells in germinal centers)+Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin (IB4 or Lycopersicon esculentum)+Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for dense mouse soft organs (5–20 mm) like the spleen, offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for whole-organ immunolabeling of B cell follicles and germinal centers. It preserves morphology with acceptable shrinkage and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes (488, 568, 594, 647) and lectins, which are robust under organic solvents. Endogenous fluorescence is quenched, so all labeling must be antibody- or dye-based. B220 labels all B cells to define follicles; GL7 marks activated B cells in germinal centers; CD35/CD21 highlights follicular dendritic cell networks within germinal centers; IB4/Lectin delineates marginal zone and vasculature for spatial context. DAPI is omitted due to compatibility cautions with target markers and FDISCO’s optional but non-essential need for nuclear counterstains when structural targets are well-defined. This multi-channel strategy enables precise 3D mapping of white pulp architecture post-vaccination.

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3 + Alexa Fluor 488, CD8 + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep, high-fidelity 3D mapping of T cell subpopulations (pan-T via CD3, cytotoxic T via CD8) within a dense, ~8 mm fixed mouse tumor. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for this tissue tier (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration essential for immunostaining in thick, lipid-rich tumors. It preserves morphology sufficiently for spatial analysis while enabling robust labeling with covalently conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes, which are compatible with iDISCO+ (unlike endogenous FPs). CD31 staining provides vascular reference without interfering with T cell signals. Nuclear counterstains (e.g., DAPI) are avoided per constraints, as they do not substitute for target-specific markers and show caution in iDISCO+.

**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-CD31 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for dense, lipid-rich mouse organs like the heart (T05 tier), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration required for whole-heart imaging of fine structures such as Purkinje fibers. CD31 immunolabeling delineates coronary vasculature for spatial reference. TO-PRO-3 was removed because nuclear counterstains like TO-PRO-3 (a DAPI/Hoechst analog) are cautioned against for Cntn2 labeling per compatibility guidelines. All signals rely on robust, covalently bound dye-conjugated antibodies, avoiding endogenous fluorescent proteins due to solvent-based quenching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for endogenous pigment reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)

9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation

10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-Cx40 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The target浦肯野纤维网络 requires specific labeling of both contactin-2 (Cntn2) and connexin 40 (Cx40), which are established molecular markers for Purkinje fibers. Given the dense, lipid-rich nature of the intact mouse heart (~10 mm scale), a high-clearing-power solvent-based method is essential. iDISCO+ provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration in whole organs of this size tier (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM), with compatibility for Alexa Fluor 568 and Alexa Fluor 647—ideal for red/far-red dual-channel imaging to minimize autofluorescence from heme and myofibrils. Endogenous fluorescence is not relied upon (no GFP/RFP reporters mentioned), so FP quenching by iDISCO+ is not a concern. Nuclear counterstains (DAPI/Hoechst) and lectins are avoided per marker-level cautions for Cx40/Cntn2 targets.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (Heme/autofluorescence removal)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Cntn2 (1:200) and anti-Cx40 (1:200) in PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two additional times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:400) in PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two additional times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
12.2 Mount cleared heart in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy using 561 nm and 640 nm laser lines.
