**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [SYCP3 + Alexa Fluor 568, DDX4/VASA + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and high refractive index matching in dense, lipid-rich organs like the mouse testis (~8 mm scale), enabling deep antibody penetration and excellent preservation of exogenous fluorophores (including Alexa Fluor dyes). It outperforms aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS) in clearing speed and depth for this tissue tier while maintaining fluorescence signal integrity. The labeling strategy targets: (1) SYCP3—a meiosis-specific marker of synaptonemal complexes—to identify and spatially map pachytene/diplotene spermatocytes across seminiferous tubule segments; and (2) DDX4/VASA—a germ cell-specific RNA helicase expressed from spermatogonia through round spermatids—to delineate the full germ cell lineage and tubule architecture. Both chosen markers are target-specific for 曲细精管/精子发生, and their fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 568 and Alexa Fluor 647) are fully compatible with FDISCO per compatibility data. DAPI was removed as it is not a target-specific label and is unnecessary given the cellular resolution provided by the two specific markers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.6 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-SYCP3 (1:200) and anti-DDX4/VASA (1:200) diluted in PBT + 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Repeat step 3.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in PBT + 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

5 Post-Staining Washes  
5.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Repeat step 5.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Repeat step 6.5 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation and Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Repeat step 7.1 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
8.2 Transfer sample to fresh ECi in imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-DDX4 (VASA) + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-SYCP3 + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for lipid- and pigment-rich tissues like intact mouse testes, offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes and DAPI—unlike iDISCO+, which caused structural damage and signal loss in the user’s prior attempt due to excessive decolorization and room-temperature processing. FDISCO enables deep antibody penetration into dense seminiferous tubules and maintains multilayered spermatogenic architecture. The labeling strategy uses target-specific markers: DDX4 (VASA) for germ cells across all stages of spermatogenesis and SYCP3 for meiotic synaptonemal complexes in spermatocytes, paired with spectrally distinct, FDISCO-compatible Alexa Fluor conjugates. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain without quenching under FDISCO conditions. All steps are performed at controlled low temperatures to minimize tissue distortion and preserve cellular morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Decolorization  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-DDX4 (1:200) and anti-SYCP3 (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS) × 5 changes.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), diluted in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Wash with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS) × 5 changes.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.9%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh ethyl cinnamate.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term storage; image within 1 week for optimal signal)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Hu C/D + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The target structures—myenteric and submucosal plexuses—require specific labeling of neuronal cell bodies and pan-neuronal fibers. Hu C/D (also known as ELAVL3/4) is a well-established nuclear marker for enteric neuron somata, while PGP9.5 (UCHL1) labels the entire neuronal cytoplasm and processes, enabling visualization of both ganglia and interganglionic fiber tracts. uDISCO is selected because it is established for long, dense tubular tissues (T06 tier), provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration, achieves high refractive index matching (~1.52) suitable for light-sheet imaging, and preserves Alexa Fluor 488/647 signals effectively. Although uDISCO causes moderate tissue shrinkage, it maintains overall 3D topology critical for network analysis, and its organic solvent-based protocol is faster than aqueous alternatives for 6-cm colon segments.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigments present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Hu C/D (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-PGP9.5 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:400) diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five more times, changing solution every 1–2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Total Time: 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-Labeling Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five more times over 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Total Time: 12 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in sealed, light-protected glass container until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
12.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles and minimal mechanical stress on the tubular structure.

**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-DDX4 (VASA) + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-SYCP3 + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep, specific labeling of germ cells (via RNA helicase DDX4/VASA) and meiotic spermatocytes (via synaptonemal complex protein SYCP3) within intact, dense mouse testes (~8 mm). iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM tissues, offering strong delipidation and high optical clarity with excellent penetration for antibody-conjugated dyes. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling relies on exogenous immunostaining with Alexa Fluor 488/568—both compatible with iDISCO+. DAPI is included cautiously as a nuclear counterstain to resolve seminiferous epithelium layering and nuclear morphology, consistent with protocol adaptations in reproductive tissue clearing. This combination enables 3D mapping of spermatogenic waves, meiotic zones, and tubule architecture.

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for pigment-rich testes)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 6 buffer changes)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in PBT + 5% donkey serum + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 6 buffer changes)  
8.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Nuclear Counterstaining  
9.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, 3 changes)  

10 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, sealed from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

13 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
13.2 Mount cleared testis in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-RBPMS + Alexa Fluor 488, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The intact mouse eyeball is a dense, pigment-rich (RPE), and lipid-containing organ that requires a high-clearing-power method for deep imaging of retinal structures. iDISCO+ provides strong delipidation and refractive index homogenization suitable for whole-eye clearing, enabling deep penetration of antibodies and dyes while effectively reducing light scattering from melanin and lipids. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, the use of exogenous immunolabeling with Alexa Fluor dyes—known to be compatible with iDISCO+—ensures robust signal retention. RBPMS is a highly specific nuclear marker for retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), and IB4 (Isolectin B4) binds specifically to endothelial glycocalyx in retinal vasculature, making this dual-labeling strategy ideal for simultaneously visualizing RGC somata and vascular networks in 3D within the intact globe.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for RPE pigment reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-RBPMS primary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two additional times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

7 Secondary Antibody and IB4 Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated IB4 (10 µg/mL) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two additional times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer cleared eyeball into glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh DBE; seal to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for ≤1 week)

**Justification:** The scientific goal requires dual labeling of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) using two independent, target-specific molecular markers—Brn3a (a canonical RGC transcription factor) and RBPMS (a highly specific cytoplasmic RGC marker)—to cross-validate identity, distribution, and cell counts. The method preserves sufficient morphology for layer-resolved 3D quantification and enables high-contrast imaging of both nuclear-localized (Brn3a) and cytoplasmic (RBPMS) signals in the ganglion cell layer without dissection.

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

6.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)

7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated donkey anti-goat IgG (1:400) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)

9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-RBPMS + Alexa Fluor 488, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The problem requires high-fidelity 3D mapping of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and superficial vasculature in intact, fixed mouse eyes (~3–4 mm), which are dense, lipid-rich, and pigmented—posing high clearing difficulty. iDISCO+ is an established organic solvent-based method for whole-eye clearing that provides strong delipidation and deep dye penetration while preserving overall morphology sufficiently for spatial correlation analyses. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, this is not a limitation here since labeling relies on exogenous dyes. RBPMS is a highly specific nuclear marker for RGCs, and IB4 (Isolectin B4) robustly labels murine retinal vascular endothelium without requiring genetic models. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 are compatible with iDISCO+ and offer bright, photostable signals ideal for light-sheet or confocal imaging of cleared tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional but recommended for eye pigment)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Blocking and Permeabilization  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-RBPMS (rabbit polyclonal, 1:200) + IB4 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (10 µg/mL) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle shaking)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Wash with PBT (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
6.2 Extended wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining (if primary is unconjugated; here required for RBPMS)  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Wash with PBT (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
8.2 Extended wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until transparent)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer cleared eyeball into glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh DBE, orient cornea-down or as needed for optical access to retina.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in sealed container for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [RBPMS + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647, IB4 (Lectin) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The problem requires strong pigment removal (especially RPE melanin), deep penetration for dual labeling of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and vasculature, and high clearing power for intact ~4 mm mouse eyes. iDISCO+—an organic solvent–based method—is established for whole-eye clearing, effectively removes lipofuscin/melanin via methanol/H₂O₂ treatment, achieves excellent refractive index matching, and enables robust antibody/dye penetration. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in iDISCO+, so we avoid GFP/RFP reporters and instead use validated target-specific primary antibodies (RBPMS for RGCs; CD31 for endothelial cells) combined with compatible Alexa Fluor dyes. IB4 lectin (conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568) provides complementary vascular lumen labeling with high specificity in retina. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568/647) are compatible with iDISCO+ and resist quenching during dehydration and delipidation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Pigment Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-RBPMS (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:100), and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated IB4 (10 µg/mL) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.2 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.3 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.4 Final PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
8.2 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
8.3 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
8.4 Final PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

12 Storage and Imaging  
12.1 Store samples immersed in DBE at RT in the dark until imaging. Mount in glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

**Justification:** FDISCO is a rapid, high-clearing-power solvent-based method compatible with small (1–5 mm) fixed brain organoids, enabling deep penetration of antibodies and dyes while preserving 3D morphology with minimal distortion relative to other organic solvent methods. It is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes and supports robust labeling of proliferation (Ki67) and overall cytoarchitecture (F-actin via Phalloidin). DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific markers for either "大脑类器官整体" or "增殖细胞核," and its inclusion violates the requirement for target-specific labeling. This combination fulfills all labeling requirements with appropriate target-specific markers and compatible fluorophores, supporting structural integrity, proliferative status, and spatial context within cleared organoids in a time-efficient manner.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (post-PFA fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (MeOH) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.6 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.3 M glycine (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining (Ki67)  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Ki67 primary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBST + 5% NDS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBST (3 × 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining

4.2 Wash with PBST (3 × 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

5 Dehydration

5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol aqueous solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Delipidation and Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Ki67 + Alexa Fluor 488, PCNA + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and high refractive index matching in dense tissues like brain organoids (1–5 mm), enabling deep antibody penetration and excellent signal-to-background for nuclear proliferation markers. It preserves synthetic fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes, which are compatible with both the targets (Ki67 and PCNA) and the FDISCO chemistry. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains (DAPI/Hoechst/PI) are not target-specific labeling for either "大脑类器官整体" or "增殖细胞核" per protocol constraints, and marker-level cautions advise against combining DAPI with Ki67 or PCNA. All signals rely on immunostaining with validated target-specific antibodies conjugated to FDISCO-compatible fluorophores, ensuring specificity, deep penetration, and minimal background—critical for high-fidelity 3D imaging of proliferation in intact organoids.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Fixation and Storage  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS, freshly prepared from powder. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.3 Store in PBS at 4 ℃ until processing (max 1 week).  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Ki67 (1:200) and anti-PCNA (1:200) diluted in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

4 Washing After Primary Antibodies  
4.1 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in blocking solution, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing After Secondary Antibodies  
6.1 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation and Bleaching  
8.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

9 Organic Solvent Transition  
9.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) mixture of 100% methanol and dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, stabilized with amylene). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh ECi. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage up to 1 week at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Ki67 + Alexa Fluor 488, PCNA + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for rapid, high-clearing-power processing of small (1–5 mm) dense tissues like brain organoids, with excellent preservation of exogenous fluorophores (including Alexa Fluor dyes). It minimizes structural fragmentation compared to harsher solvent methods (e.g., uDISCO/iDISCO+) by incorporating stabilizing dehydration steps and avoids the slow kinetics of aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC), which likely contributed to prior structural collapse. The dual-proliferation labeling strategy uses two orthogonal cell-cycle markers—Ki67 (expressed in all active phases) and PCNA (S-phase enriched)—conjugated to spectrally distinct, FDISCO-compatible Alexa Fluor dyes, enabling robust quantification of proliferative states. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific markers for either “大脑类器官整体” or “增殖细胞核,” and its inclusion violates the requirement for target-specific labeling. This combination supports high-throughput, low-distortion 3D imaging of drug effects on organoid growth and proliferation using validated, compatible reagents.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling (permeabilization and staining integrated)  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Ki67 (1:200) and anti-PCNA (1:200) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Wash with 100% methanol (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568 donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.6 Wash with 100% methanol (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) hydrogen peroxide in 100% methanol (prepare fresh: 1 vol 30% H₂O₂ + 9 vol MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.3 Wash with 100% methanol (2 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

4 Final Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer cleared organoids into glass vials filled with ethyl cinnamate (ECi) and seal.(Temperature: RT, protected from light, Time: until imaging)  
6.2 Mount directly in ECi-compatible imaging chambers for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional washing.

6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

8.1 Transfer cleared organoids into glass vials filled with ethyl cinnamate (ECi) and seal.(Temperature: RT, protected from light, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, Keratin 14 (K14) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The clinical human skin biopsy is a dense, lipid-rich tissue requiring strong clearing with minimal morphological distortion to accurately quantify epidermal nerve fiber (IENF) architecture. MACS is an aqueous-based method established for T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK samples, offering excellent antibody penetration, preservation of fine neurite morphology, and compatibility with both Alexa Fluor 488 (for PGP9.5, the gold-standard pan-neuronal marker for IENF in clinical diagnostics) and Alexa Fluor 647 (for K14 to delineate epidermal boundaries). Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., uDISCO/iDISCO+), MACS avoids tissue shrinkage and preserves 3D geometry critical for IENF density and branching analysis. DAPI/Hoechst are excluded as they do not label IENFs and could introduce background; K14 provides essential epidermal reference without interfering with neural signal.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (10% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and rabbit anti-Keratin 14 (1:300) in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 6 changes over 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 6 changes over 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

2 Dehydration (optional pre-clearing equilibration for aqueous clearing)  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Rehydration: reverse series (80% → 60% → 40% → 20% methanol in PBS, 30 min each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  

3 Optical Clearing with MACS  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Equilibration in fresh MACS-R2 for imaging compatibility. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry/RFP]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically validated for small whole organisms like C. elegans, offering excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and mCherry/RFP), minimal morphological distortion, and sufficient refractive index matching for high-resolution 3D imaging of neural structures. Given that the sample already expresses cell-type-specific EGFP and mCherry/RFP reporters in neurons, no additional immunostaining or exogenous dyes are required, simplifying the workflow while maintaining signal fidelity for dual-color visualization of distinct neuronal populations within the intact nervous system.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Wash  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST) to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Repeat PBST wash once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Ce3D Clearing Solution Preparation and Incubation  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.5% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-A solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (62.5% (wt/vol) fructose, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.5% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 7.4; final RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-B solution until sample becomes optically transparent (typically judged by loss of light scattering under stereomicroscope).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12–24 hours)  

4 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer cleared worm into a glass-bottom imaging dish or chambered coverglass pre-filled with Ce3D-B solution to maintain RI matching during imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or store at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The clinical human skin biopsy is a dense, lipid-rich tissue requiring strong yet morphology-preserving clearing with deep antibody/dye penetration. MACS is an aqueous-based method established for T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK samples, offering excellent preservation of tissue architecture (minimal shrinkage), compatibility with multiple Alexa Fluor dyes, and low toxicity—critical for clinical specimens. PGP9.5 is the gold-standard pan-neuronal marker for intraepidermal nerve fibers (IENF) in human skin pathology; CD31 provides specific endothelial labeling of dermal vasculature. Both labels are target-specific and compatible with MACS per domain records. IB4 was removed due to marker-level cautions against lectin use with PGP9.5 and CD31 targets, ensuring strict adherence to target-specific labeling requirements. Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 are fully compatible with MACS and avoid all listed incompatibilities.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Fixation and Storage  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS, pH 7.4. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.3 Store in PBS at 4 ℃ until processing (max 1 week).  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution: 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-CD31 (1:200) diluted in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) for PGP9.5, Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500) for CD31, both diluted in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Post-labeling Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  

7 Dehydration (Optional Pre-Clearing Step for Aqueous Methods)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

8 Rehydration  
8.1 Reverse rehydration through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  
8.2 Final wash in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Optical Clearing with MACS  
9.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
9.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

10.1 Transfer sample to fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage or immediate imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), mCherry/RFP (内源)]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically validated for small whole specimens like C. elegans (~1 mm), offering excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and mCherry/RFP), minimal morphological distortion, and sufficient refractive index matching for high-resolution 3D imaging of neural structures such as the nerve ring and ventral nerve cord. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), Ce3D avoids organic solvents that quench or denature fluorescent proteins, which is critical since the scientific goal relies entirely on intrinsic dual-color FP reporters. Additionally, Ce3D provides adequate tissue transparency within a reasonable timeframe for nematode-scale samples while maintaining compatibility with standard confocal or light-sheet microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in alcohol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.4 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

2 Ce3D Clearing Solution Preparation and Incubation  
2.1 Prepare Ce3D clearing solution: 10% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (NMN), 25% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water (final pH ~7.0)  
2.2 Incubation with freshly prepared Ce3D solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Transfer samples to Ce3D-RI matching solution: 63% (wt/vol) iodixanol (OptiPrep™) in Ce3D base buffer (without Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Mount individual C. elegans adults in glass-bottom imaging chambers using Ce3D-RI matching solution as immersion medium (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Human skin biopsies are lipid- and pigment-rich (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH), requiring a high-clearing-power solvent-based method with deep antibody penetration and minimal signal quenching. FDISCO is ideal: it preserves synthetic fluorophores (Alexa Fluor dyes), enables robust delipidation for dense dermal tissue, and achieves high refractive index matching suitable for confocal/light-sheet imaging of 2–3 mm thick samples. PGP9.5 is the gold-standard pan-neuronal marker for IENF quantification in clinical dermatopathology; CD31 labels endothelial cells to reconstruct superficial dermal vasculature. Hoechst was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific labeling per domain requirements, and although FDISCO lists Hoechst as compatible, its use violates the target-specificity rule for the required labeling targets. All remaining fluorophores are explicitly compatible with FDISCO per domain records.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash fixed biopsy (3–4 mm diameter, 2–3 mm thick, 4% PFA-fixed) 3× with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash)  
1.2 Block in blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for permeabilization and non-specific binding reduction. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibodies: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and rat anti-CD31 (1:200) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.4 Wash 5× with PBST to remove unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rat IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.6 Wash 5× with PBST to remove unbound secondaries. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours in dark)  
3.2 Wash 2× with 100% methanol to remove residual H₂O₂. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min per wash)  

4 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain verification; skip if Hoechst signal sufficient)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Dehydration (second round, prior to RI matching)  
5.1 Repeat steps 2.1–2.6 exactly as above. (Temperature: RT, Time: as specified in Step 2)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and dibenzyl ether (DBE). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (e.g., Sigma 108014-1KG). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.3 Transfer to fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite; store in dark at RT)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry/RFP]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically validated for small whole organisms like C. elegans, offering excellent preservation of endogenous EGFP and mCherry/RFP fluorescence without quenching—critical for dual-color neuronal tracing. It minimizes tissue distortion (<5% shrinkage), maintains fine neural structures such as the ~1-μm-diameter neurites in the nerve ring, and achieves refractive index (RI) matching within 24–48 hours, enabling rapid 3D confocal or light-sheet imaging. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), Ce3D avoids organic solvents that denature fluorescent proteins. Among aqueous methods compatible with T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM, Ce3D provides superior antibody/dye penetration if future immunolabeling is needed, though here we rely solely on genetically encoded EGFP and mCherry/RFP reporters as specified.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Wash  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Optical Clearing with Ce3D Reagents  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-A solution for complete lipid extraction and initial RI homogenization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) for final RI matching (~1.46). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Transfer sample into a glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary filled with fresh Ce3D-B solution for immediate imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour equilibration before imaging)  
3.2 Seal sample chamber with vacuum grease or coverslip to prevent evaporation during long-term 3D acquisition. (Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for high-pigment, lipid-rich tissues like human skin biopsies, offering strong delipidation and melanin reduction while preserving antibody-based fluorescence signals. It effectively clears dense dermal collagen and reduces melanin-induced background without excessive tissue shrinkage when applied to small biopsies (3–4 mm). The chosen markers—PGP9.5 (a gold-standard pan-neuronal marker for IENF in clinical diagnostics) and CD31 (a specific endothelial marker for superficial dermal vasculature)—are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent workflow. Alexa Fluor 647 and Alexa Fluor 488 are both highly stable under FDISCO conditions and provide spectrally distinct, high-contrast channels for simultaneous 3D visualization of IENFs and vascular reference structures. This dual-labeling strategy enables reliable spatial registration of nerve fibers relative to vascular landmarks, improving IENF density quantification accuracy.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-CD31/PECAM1 (1:200) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (3 changes, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, dark)  
1.5 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (3 changes, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Melanin Reduction  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (2 changes, 30 minutes each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)  

4 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Organic Solvent Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (RI ≈ 1.558). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours or until optically transparent)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate. (Temperature: RT, storage in dark)  
6.2 Mount in custom imaging chamber with ECi as immersion medium for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

The chosen markers—PGP9.5 (a gold-standard pan-neuronal marker for IENF in clinical diagnostics) and CD31 (a specific endothelial marker for superficial dermal vasculature)—are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent workflow. Alexa Fluor 647 and Alexa Fluor 488 are both highly stable under FDISCO conditions and provide spectrally distinct, high-contrast channels for simultaneous 3D visualization of IENFs and vascular reference structures. This dual-labeling strategy enables reliable spatial registration of nerve fibers relative to vascular landmarks, improving IENF density quantification accuracy.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking/permeabilization buffer: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-CD31/PECAM1 (1:200) diluted in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (3 changes, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, dark)  
1.5 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (3 changes, 1 hour each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Melanin Reduction  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (2 changes, 30 minutes each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)  

4 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Organic Solvent Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (RI ≈ 1.558). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours or until optically transparent)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate. (Temperature: RT, storage in dark)  
6.2 Mount in custom imaging chamber with ECi as immersion medium for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry/RFP]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically validated for small whole organisms like C. elegans (tier T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM). It preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and mCherry/RFP) without quenching, maintains native tissue morphology with minimal shrinkage or distortion, and allows sufficient penetration for high-resolution 3D imaging of internal neural structures such as the nerve ring and ventral nerve cord. Given that the transgenic lines already express cell-type-specific EGFP and mCherry/RFP reporters labeling distinct neuronal populations, no additional immunostaining or exogenous dyes are required for primary structural mapping. However, if nuclear context is needed for spatial referencing, Hoechst can be optionally included without compromising FP signal.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) to ensure complete fixation if not already performed.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

2 Optional Nuclear Counterstain (if spatial reference needed)  
2.1 Incubation with 5 μg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

3 Dehydration (Gradual Glycerol Equilibration)  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Primary Clearing with Ce3D Reagent A  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D Reagent A (8 M urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH adjusted to 7.5 with NaOH).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Clearing with Ce3D Reagent B  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D Reagent B (8 M urea, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with Ce3D Mounting Solution (86% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, final RI ≈ 1.46).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer cleared worms into glass-bottom imaging chamber or capillary tube filled with fresh Ce3D Mounting Solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Primary Clearing with Ce3D Reagent A  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D Reagent A (8 M urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH adjusted to 7.5 with NaOH).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

5.1 Incubation with Ce3D Reagent B (8 M urea, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

7.1 Transfer cleared worms into glass-bottom imaging chamber or capillary tube filled with fresh Ce3D Mounting Solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole zebrafish (1–5 mm) that preserves fine cellular morphology with minimal shrinkage—critical for analyzing hair cell arrangement and stereocilia bundle geometry. It supports deep penetration of both phalloidin and antibodies while maintaining fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles with high specificity, and Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, target-specific marker for zebrafish lateral line hair cells. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific labeling and are cautioned against when used with Myosin VIIa. Ce3D’s compatibility with these fluorophores and its gentle processing make it ideal for developmental or drug-response morphological studies at 5 dpf.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody diluted 1:200 in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

4 Tissue Clearing with Ce3D  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.0) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

6 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging dish filled with Ce3D-C (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole zebrafish (1–5 mm), preserving fine cellular morphology with minimal distortion—critical for analyzing stereociliary bundle integrity and orientation. It supports deep penetration of both small-molecule dyes (e.g., Phalloidin) and antibodies, and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 568. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia without requiring genetic reporters or antibody amplification, while Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, specific marker for zebrafish lateral line hair cells. This dual-labeling strategy enables unambiguous identification of hair cells (Myosin VIIa+) and high-resolution visualization of their apical actin architecture (Phalloidin+), fulfilling the scientific goal. DAPI was removed due to marker-level cautions against nuclear counterstains for Myosin VIIa labeling.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (Myosin VIIa)  
2.1 Incubation with rabbit anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody diluted 1:200 in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
3.1 Incubation with goat anti-rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

4 Ce3D Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B (50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with Ce3D-R (88% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish and submerge in fresh Ce3D-R for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP/YFP (endogenous reporter), SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** ClearSee is an aqueous, plant-optimized clearing method specifically validated for *Arabidopsis thaliana* whole seedlings. It preserves endogenous GFP/YFP fluorescence without quenching, maintains tissue morphology with minimal distortion, and is compatible with cell wall dyes. SCRI Renaissance 2200 is a far-red fluorescent dye that selectively labels plant cell walls, providing high-contrast visualization of tissue architecture—including root zones, lateral root primordia, and vascular boundaries—without interfering with GFP/YFP signals. This combination fulfills the requirement to simultaneously image transgenic fluorescence and cellular context in intact 15–20 mm seedlings.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Cell Wall Staining  
1.1 Incubation with 0.1% (wt/vol) SCRI Renaissance 2200 in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

3 Tissue Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with ClearSee solution (10% (wt/vol) KSCN, 12% (wt/vol) glycerol, 8% (wt/vol) sorbitol in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Transfer samples to fresh ClearSee solution for final RI matching (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Mount cleared seedlings in glass-bottom imaging dishes or capillaries filled with ClearSee solution for immediate confocal or light-sheet imaging
