**Chosen Method:** ClearSee  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), YFP (内源), SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** ClearSee is an aqueous, non-toxic, and GFP/YFP-compatible optical clearing method specifically developed and validated for whole-mount *Arabidopsis thaliana* seedlings. It effectively removes chlorophyll and reduces light scattering from cell walls while preserving endogenous fluorescent protein signals—critical for observing deep-root expression of GFP/YFP reporters. SCRI Renaissance 2200 is a cell wall–specific fluorogenic dye compatible with ClearSee that labels cellulose-rich structures without requiring antibodies, enabling precise delineation of tissue boundaries and cellular layers. This combination meets the requirement to retain intrinsic fluorescence and visualize cell wall architecture in intact 15–20 mm seedlings.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.4 Incubation with distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Cell Wall Staining with SCRI Renaissance 2200  
2.1 Incubation with 10 µM SCRI Renaissance 2200 in distilled water (freshly prepared from DMSO stock; final DMSO ≤0.1%) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
2.2 Wash with distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes, protected from light)  

3 Optical Clearing with ClearSee Solution  
3.1 Incubation with ClearSee solution (10% (wt/vol) xylitol, 10% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 25% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24–48 hours, protected from light; duration depends on sample opacity—typically 36 hours for 15–20 mm seedlings)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Transfer cleared seedling to fresh ClearSee solution for imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging to equilibrate)  
4.2 Mount sample in glass-bottom dish or capillary using ClearSee solution as immersion medium (no additional RI-matching step required; ClearSee has RI ≈1.42, suitable for confocal/light-sheet imaging with standard objectives)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole zebrafish samples (1–5 mm), preserving fine cellular morphology with minimal distortion—critical for resolving hair cell stereocilia bundles and nerve fiber trajectories. It supports deep penetration of both phalloidin and antibodies while maintaining compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in hair cell apical bundles, providing high-resolution structural detail without requiring transgenic lines. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) is a well-validated marker for zebrafish lateral line nerve fibers, and its immunodetection with Alexa Fluor 568 enables specific visualization of innervation patterns. Ce3D preserves fluorescence intensity and spatial fidelity better than solvent-based methods (e.g., uDISCO), which risk shrinkage and are incompatible with delicate actin structures.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO for permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100 + 10% normal goat serum + 1% DMSO).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (for β-III Tubulin)  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody: mouse anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) diluted 1:200 in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100) three times, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibody: goat anti-mouse IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBST three times, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

4 Tissue Clearing with Ce3D  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with Ce3D-C solution (75% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
5.1 Transfer samples to final RI-matching solution: Ce3D-M (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 33% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4; RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Mount cleared larvae in Ce3D-M within glass-bottom imaging chambers or agarose molds for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor 488, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole zebrafish (T03 tier) that preserves tissue morphology with minimal swelling or distortion—addressing the user’s requirement for preserved geometry. It supports deep penetration of antibodies and phalloidin while maintaining fluorescence intensity of Alexa Fluor dyes. Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, specific marker for zebrafish lateral line hair cells, and direct labeling with Alexa Fluor–conjugated phalloidin robustly visualizes F-actin–based stereociliary bundles without requiring genetic reporters. Both labels are compatible with Ce3D and avoid reliance on endogenous FPs that may be weak or variable.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (Myosin VIIa)  
2.1 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NGS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-host secondary antibody (1:500) + Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated Phalloidin (1:100) in PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NGS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4 Tissue Optical Clearing (Ce3D)  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with Ce3D-C (75% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
5.1 Transfer samples to Ce3D-M (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 33% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4; RI ≈ 1.48) for final equilibration (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Mount intact in Ce3D-M within glass-bottom imaging chamber or agarose mold for light-sheet/confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for ≤1 week)

**Chosen Method:** ClearSee  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP/YFP (内源报告信号), SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** ClearSee is an aqueous-based, plant-optimized optical clearing method specifically validated for intact *Arabidopsis thaliana* seedlings up to 20 mm in length. It preserves endogenous GFP/YFP fluorescence without quenching—critical for analyzing native reporter expression—and is compatible with cell wall–specific dyes like SCRI Renaissance 2200, which selectively labels plant cell walls without requiring immunostaining. This combination enables simultaneous 3D visualization of tissue architecture (via SCRI R2200) and spatially resolved transgene expression (via GFP/YFP) across all root zones (epidermis, cortex, endodermis, vasculature, meristem) in deep tissue, fulfilling the scientific goal of correlating expression patterns with anatomical context.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Sample Preparation and Rehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 1× PBS (phosphate-buffered saline, pH 7.4) to wash out fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) glycerol in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Cell Wall Staining with SCRI Renaissance 2200  
2.1 Incubation with 0.1% (wt/vol) SCRI Renaissance 2200 in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
2.2 Wash with 1× PBS (three changes, 30 minutes each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

3 Optical Clearing with ClearSee Solution  
3.1 Incubation with ClearSee solution (10% (wt/vol) KI, 15% (wt/vol) NaI, 25% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Transfer sample into fresh ClearSee solution for final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Mount cleared seedling in a glass-bottom imaging dish or chamber filled with ClearSee solution for immediate light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: proceed to imaging)

我需要对植物系统中的拟南芥完整幼苗进行透明化处理，用于观察根系深层 GFP/YFP 转基因荧光报告信号，并同时显示细胞壁结构。样本为完整幼苗，长度约 15–20 mm，包括根、下胚轴和茎叶，已完成固定和后固定。科学目标是在透明化后尽量保留 GFP/YFP 内源荧光报告信号，降低叶绿素和组织散射带来的背景，同时用细胞壁染料显示根、茎叶和维管组织的细胞轮廓，便于判断报告信号所在的组织层次和细胞位置。

**Chosen Method:** TDE  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP/YFP (endogenous), SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** TDE is an aqueous, refractive index–tunable clearing method established for whole Arabidopsis seedlings (T11_PLANT_WHOLE_SEEDLING) that preserves endogenous GFP/YFP fluorescence without quenching, unlike organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). It effectively reduces light scattering while maintaining tissue integrity. Although dye penetration in TDE is moderate, SCRI Renaissance 2200—a cell wall–specific fluorescent dye compatible with aqueous environments and shown to label plant cell walls robustly—can be efficiently delivered during the clearing process. TDE also enables gradual RI matching suitable for confocal or light-sheet imaging of 15–20 mm samples, and its protocol can be optimized with extended incubation to enhance chlorophyll removal and transparency beyond standard ClearSee.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Wash  
1.1 Incubation with 1× PBS (phosphate-buffered saline, pH 7.2) to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Chlorophyll Bleaching and Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 5% (wt/vol) sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in 1× PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh 5% (wt/vol) SDS in 1× PBS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Cell Wall Staining with SCRI Renaissance 2200  
3.1 Incubation with 10 µg/mL SCRI Renaissance 2200 in 1× PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 1× PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 (3 changes, 2 hours each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

4 Refractive Index Matching via TDE Series  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) TDE (2,2′-thiodiethanol) in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) TDE in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) TDE in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) TDE in 1× PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with 97% (vol/vol) TDE (final RI ~1.52). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer cleared seedlings into glass-bottom imaging dishes filled with 97% TDE. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 1 week, protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for dense soft tissues like skeletal muscle, offering high refractive index matching, strong lipid removal, and excellent preservation of dye-based fluorescence—including Alexa Fluor dyes—while minimizing signal quenching. It is established for mouse soft organs in the 5–20 mm size range and provides rapid, deep penetration suitable for thick (~3 mm)腓肠肌 samples. Alpha-bungarotoxin directly and specifically labels acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) at the postsynaptic membrane without requiring antibodies, preserving fine structural details of NMJ morphology. Co-labeling with TUJ1 (β-III Tubulin) via Alexa Fluor 488 allows visualization of motor axon terminals to contextualize NMJ spatial organization. Both fluorophores (Alexa 488 and 647) are fully compatible with FDISCO per compatibility data, ensuring robust signal retention through dehydration and delipidation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-Clearing Staining  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (1 µg/mL) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 4 changes, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours total)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi) for long-term storage or immediate imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibody]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for dense mouse soft tissues (5–20 mm scale), offering strong delipidation and deep dye/antibody penetration required for intact skeletal muscle. It effectively clears myofiber-rich tissue while preserving NMJ morphology with minimal autofluorescence. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses exogenous dyes: α-bungarotoxin directly and specifically labels postsynaptic AChR clusters (gold standard for NMJ postsynaptic labeling), and β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) robustly marks motor axons and nerve terminals. Both Alexa Fluor 647 and Alexa Fluor 488 are fully compatible with iDISCO+. This combination enables high-resolution 3D co-visualization of pre- and postsynaptic NMJ components for quantitative analysis of alignment, coverage, fragmentation, and spatial distribution.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and 0.3% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (wt/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (for motor nerve terminals)  
2.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) mouse monoclonal antibody diluted 1:500 in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100, 0.02% sodium azide in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PTwH buffer (0.1% Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin in PBS) three times, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody and α-Bungarotoxin Co-Staining  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated α-bungarotoxin (1 μg/mL) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PTwH buffer three times, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Rehydration (optional intermediate step for RI matching transition)  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for initial clearing.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Sample Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer cleared muscle into a glass imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE and seal with coverslip-compatible adhesive.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong lipid removal and high refractive index matching in dense tissues like skeletal muscle, while preserving exogenous fluorescent dyes such as Alexa Fluor conjugates—critical given the user’s prior issue with weak alpha-bungarotoxin signal after THF/DBE. Unlike iDISCO+, FDISCO explicitly preserves Alexa Fluor 488/568/647 signals and minimizes fluorescence quenching. It also offers better morphological retention than uDISCO or PEGASOS for soft organs in the 5–20 mm range, reducing the severe shrinkage previously observed. For labeling: alpha-bungarotoxin directly and specifically binds acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) at the postsynaptic membrane, fulfilling the requirement for a target-specific marker for 突触后膜/AChR 聚集; when conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (far-red), it resists solvent-induced quenching in FDISCO. β-III Tubulin (recognized by TUJ1 antibody) is a well-established, target-specific marker for the axonal cytoskeleton in motor nerve terminals (运动神经末梢/轴突骨架); pairing it with Alexa Fluor 488 ensures compatibility with FDISCO’s dye preservation profile and enables clear distinction from AChR signal. This dual-labeling strategy fulfills the scientific goal of assessing NMJ pairing, fragmentation, and denervation without introducing non-permitted markers.  

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining (for motor nerve axons)  
2.1 Incubation with anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody diluted 1:500 in antibody dilution buffer (1% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody and Alpha-Bungarotoxin Co-Staining  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (1 µg/mL) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Transfer to fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi) for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires deep, uniform labeling of the entire gastric neural plexus across all wall layers in a relatively large (~20 mm), dense soft organ. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for mouse soft organs of this size tier (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM), offering strong delipidation power, rapid clearing kinetics, and excellent antibody penetration—critical for thick-tissue immunolabeling of pan-neuronal markers. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched by iDISCO+, so we use robust, covalently conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes compatible with the protocol. PGP9.5 and β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) are validated target-specific markers for the gastric enteric/parasympathetic nerve network; dual labeling ensures comprehensive coverage of both mature fibers (PGP9.5) and growing/structural microtubules (TUJ1). Phalloidin was removed because it is not a target-specific marker for the required labeling target (gastric vagal/pan-neural fiber network) and constitutes structural context staining that does not fulfill the target-specific requirement. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488 and 647) are explicitly compatible with iDISCO+.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for pigmented stomach tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 6 buffer changes)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 6 buffer changes, protected from light)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging, protected from light)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in the dark. Image within 7 days using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission filters for Alexa Fluor 488 and 647.

**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D mapping of the entire gastric wall neural plexus—including fine nerve terminals—across a thick (~8 mm), multi-layered organ. PGP9.5 and β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) are well-established pan-neuronal markers that robustly label both myelinated/unmyelinated fibers and terminal arborizations in the enteric and vagal innervation of the stomach. **Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), tdTomato (内源)]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous EGFP and tdTomato fluorescence to trace long-range projections from specific neuronal populations in the amygdala–prefrontal cortex–thalamus–nucleus accumbens circuit. MACS is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method that is fully compatible with both EGFP and tdTomato, avoids organic solvents that quench fluorescent proteins, and provides sufficient clearing depth for intact adult mouse brains (~10 mm scale). It enables high-fidelity 3D visualization of fine axonal processes without requiring antibody amplification for the primary tracers, thus preserving native expression patterns and minimizing processing artifacts.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Optional Permeabilization Enhancement (for dense tissue)  
3.1 Incubation with PBST + 4% (wt/vol) sucrose (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Primary Clearing (Delipidation & Refractive Index Homogenization)  
4.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide [MXDA], 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 36 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with MACS-Matching Solution (60 vol% MXDA, 60% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

6 Final Equilibration for Imaging  
6.1 Transfer brain to fresh MACS-Matching Solution in imaging-compatible glass-bottom dish or capillary (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour prior to imaging)  

7 Storage (if not imaged immediately)  
7.1 Store sample immersed in MACS-Matching Solution at 4 ℃ in the dark (stable for ≥2 weeks with minimal fluorescence loss)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The mouse stomach is a dense, lipid-rich soft organ (~20 mm scale) requiring strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—iDISCO+ excels in these aspects with rapid, high-clearing power for whole organs of this size tier. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are not specified, so we rely on robust immunolabeling. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) is the gold standard for labeling enteric and vagal nerve fibers in the gut wall and is compatible with organic solvent-based clearing when paired with Alexa Fluor 647 (highly stable in iDISCO+). Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 provides high-fidelity F-actin labeling to resolve circular/longitudinal muscle layers as structural references; Alexa Fluor 488 is confirmed compatible with iDISCO+. Nuclear counterstains are avoided per marker cautions for PGP9.5.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for autofluorescence reduction in gastric tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 5% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-PGP9.5 primary antibody (e.g., Abcam ab108986 or equivalent) diluted 1:500 in PBT + 5% NDS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washes Post Primary  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 three more times, changing solution every 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit (or appropriate host) secondary antibody (1:500) + Alexa Fluor 488 Phalloidin (1:100) in PBT + 5% NDS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Washes Post Staining  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 three more times, changing solution every 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
12.2 Mount cleared stomach in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), tdTomato (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous EGFP/tdTomato signals for long-range projection tracing across amygdala, prefrontal cortex, thalamus, and nucleus accumbens, while simultaneously visualizing local dendritic arborization. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method compatible with endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and tdTomato), provides excellent tissue transparency for whole adult mouse brains (~10 mm scale), and supports deep antibody penetration without quenching or significant distortion. Among pan-neuronal structural markers, MAP2 specifically labels dendrites and soma (not axons), making it ideal for resolving dendritic architecture in target regions. Conjugation to Alexa Fluor 647 ensures spectral separation from EGFP (green) and tdTomato (red) and is fully compatible with MACS. This combination enables simultaneous imaging of endogenous projection tracers and immunolabeled dendritic scaffolds in a single cleared brain.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (e.g., mouse monoclonal, 1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (1% NGS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 12 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 changes, 12 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to final imaging medium: MACS-R2 (same as 2.3) in glass vial with minimal headspace (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging; stable for months at 4 ℃ in dark)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The mouse stomach is a dense, lipid-rich soft organ (~20 mm scale) requiring strong delipidation and high refractive index matching for deep imaging of fine neural processes. iDISCO+ provides rapid, high-clearing power with excellent antibody penetration in whole organs of this size tier (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM). It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647—robust synthetic fluorophores resistant to organic solvents—and avoids reliance on endogenous FPs (which are quenched). PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) and β-III Tubulin/TUJ1 (a neuron-specific cytoskeletal marker) together comprehensively label all neuronal fibers, including fine vagal terminals, across gastric layers. Both are valid target-specific markers for 胃壁迷走神经/泛神经纤维网络 per the knowledge base. The dual-labeling strategy enables discrimination of fiber morphology and spatial coverage without spectral overlap. Rigorous pre-permeabilization, blocking, and extended washes in iDISCO+ mitigate the high background previously observed.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat 8.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat 10.2 once with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours or until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP/tdTomato (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous EGFP/tdTomato fluorescence to trace long-range projections from emotion-related regions (e.g., amygdala → NAc/thalamus), while simultaneously visualizing local neuronal processes (dendrites/axons) in target zones for spatial correlation. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that robustly preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and tdTomato) and supports deep antibody penetration in whole adult mouse brains (~10 mm scale). Among compatible pan-neuronal structural markers, MAP2 specifically labels dendrites and somatodendritic compartments—ideal for resolving projection terminal apposition to local dendritic arbors—without interfering with nuclear or synaptic markers. Alexa Fluor 647 is highly compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from EGFP/tdTomato, enabling multichannel 3D imaging. Solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) were excluded due to risk of FP quenching; MACS balances FP preservation, clearing efficacy, and immunolabeling depth for this application.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (performed before clearing to ensure antibody penetration)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or rabbit, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 changes over 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours per wash, protected from light)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours, gentle agitation)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle agitation)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle agitation)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer cleared brain into fresh MACS-R2 in a light-protected imaging chamber (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging)  
3.2 Store long-term in MACS-R2 at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 4 weeks without signal degradation.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), tdTomato (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous EGFP/tdTomato signals and robust labeling of dendritic architecture across a large, lipid-rich adult mouse whole brain. SWITCH failed due to insufficient delipidation and poor far-red antibody penetration. Among compatible methods, MACS is an aqueous-based clearing technique that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including EGFP and tdTomato), enables deep antibody penetration into dense tissue, provides uniform refractive index (RI) matching up to ~1.51, and avoids organic solvents that quench fluorescence or cause shrinkage. MAP2 is listed as a valid marker candidate for both "神经元(通用)" and "CA1 树突/树突棘结构辅助" targets per the knowledge base, and Alexa Fluor 647 is fully compatible with MACS for far-red imaging with low background. This combination satisfies the need for simultaneous visualization of long-range projections (via endogenous FP) and local dendritic structure (via anti-MAP2-AF647).  

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (e.g., Millipore AB5622 or equivalent) diluted 1:200 in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 5 changes over 2 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:300 in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 5 changes over 2 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0: 20% (vol/vol) MXDA (N-methyldiethanolamine), 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours, gentle agitation)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle agitation)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2: 40% (vol/vol) MXDA, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, gentle agitation)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Incubation with final RI-matching solution: MACS-R2 (same as 2.3) for equilibration (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Store sample in MACS-R2 at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging; mount directly in MACS-R2 for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires tracing two distinct somatosensory projection pathways across large, lipid-rich CNS tissues (3 cm spinal cord, thalamus, and cortical slabs). DiI and DiD are lipophilic carbocyanine dyes that stably incorporate into neuronal membranes and are ideal for long-range axonal tracing without requiring genetic manipulation or immunostaining. uDISCO is a solvent-based whole-organ clearing method specifically validated for long CNS tracts (T06_LONG_CNS_OR_TUBULAR_15_80MM tier), offering high delipidation power, deep dye preservation, and compatibility with DiI/DiD fluorescence. It achieves strong refractive index matching for light-sheet imaging while maintaining signal integrity over centimeter-scale distances—critical for reconstructing 3D somatosensory circuits from periphery to cortex.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if tissue pigmentation present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma D108014).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer cleared samples to glass vials filled with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether and store at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite until imaging)  
5.2 Prior to light-sheet or confocal imaging, equilibrate sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber for ≥30 minutes to minimize RI mismatch artifacts.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-c-Fos + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-NeuN + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires detection of activity-dependent neuronal ensembles (via immediate early gene c-Fos) across multiple deep brain nuclei and preservation of the tongue–brain spatial relationship in a large, dense tissue block. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for tier T06_LONG_CNS_OR_TUBULAR_15_80MM samples, offering strong delipidation power, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched by iDISCO+, so immunolabeling with Alexa Fluor–conjugated secondary antibodies is essential. c-Fos is a validated activity-dependent marker for anesthesia–awakening paradigms; NeuN provides pan-neuronal context without substituting for functional labeling. TO-PRO-3 was removed as it is a nuclear counterstain not specific to the target and is listed under marker-level cautions for c-Fos and NeuN. This combination enables quantitative 3D mapping of activated neurons within intact neuroanatomical circuits.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented tissue; include for tongue melanin)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two additional times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining

8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two additional times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Final Wash

**Justification:** The scientific goal requires dual detection of two immediate early genes (IEGs)—c-Fos and Npas4—to map activity-dependent neuronal ensembles across deep brain nuclei (MTN, LC, PVT, NAcSh) in intact brain-tongue specimens. iDISCO+ is an established solvent-based clearing method for large, dense tissues (T06 tier), offering strong delipidation, deep antibody penetration, and compatibility with Alexa Fluor 488/647—both robust against organic solvents and critical for low-background, high-signal dual labeling. Unlike aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS), iDISCO+ achieves faster, more uniform clearing in lipid-rich brain and muscular tongue tissue while preserving antigenicity when proper rehydration and blocking are applied. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched by iDISCO+, but since the experiment relies on IEG immunostaining (not transgenic reporters), this is not a limitation. The protocol includes graded dehydration/rehydration, extended permeabilization, blocking, and multi-day antibody incubations to ensure deep, specific labeling with minimal background.

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented tongue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with PBT + 10% (wt/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-c-Fos (rabbit, 1:500) and anti-Npas4 (goat, 1:250) diluted in PBT + 5% NDS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Washes  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBT + 5% NDS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Post-Labeling Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 2:1 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires tracing two distinct long-range somatosensory pathways through dense, lipid-rich CNS tissue (spinal cord, thalamus, cortex) over distances >15 mm. DiI and DiD are lipophilic carbocyanine dyes ideal for anterograde/retrograde axonal tracing with minimal diffusion, high photostability, and compatibility with organic solvent–based clearing. uDISCO provides strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for deep imaging of large, fixed CNS specimens, while preserving DiI/DiD fluorescence. NeuN (RBFOX3) is a pan-neuronal nuclear marker and does not specifically label the somatosensory ascending pathway; thus, it violates target-specificity requirements and has been removed. uDISCO is established for T06_LONG_CNS_OR_TUBULAR_15_80MM samples and supports robust dye penetration without requiring immunostaining for pathway identification.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigment present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Repeat step 3.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Store samples immersed in DBE in glass vials protected from light at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
5.2 Mount sample in a DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

我需要对小鼠完整脊髓、丘脑和体感皮层进行整体透明化处理，用于研究躯体感觉信息从外周到中枢的传递通路。样本包括约 3 cm 长完整脊髓、约 5 mm × 4 mm × 4 mm 的丘脑和约 1 cm × 0.8 cm × 2 mm 的体感皮层组织，已完成固定和后固定。科学目标是使用两种脂溶性示踪染料追踪不同感觉通路的神经投射，比较它们在脊髓、丘脑和体感皮层中的走行、终末分布和通路分离/重叠关系。

我在进行小鼠脊髓-丘脑-皮层感觉通路透明化实验时遇到问题：固定后直接放入 SDS 清除液中处理 48 小时，然后进行 Alexa Fluor 647 孵育 24 小时，最后放入甘油中。结果组织仍然不透明，且 Alexa Fluor 647 信号分布不均匀。该流程与科学目标不匹配，因为目标是保留并成像 DiI/DiD 脂溶性示踪信号，而不是依赖 Alexa Fluor 抗体孵育；同时 SDS 48 小时和甘油匹配不足以完成长脊髓和脑区组织的均一透明化。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法。修正版应适合 DiI/DiD 脂溶性示踪信号保留、长程感觉通路成像、脊髓和脑区组织充分脱水/脱脂、低背景、均一 RI 匹配和三维重建。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires long-range tracing of somatosensory pathways using lipophilic carbocyanine dyes (DiI/DiD), which are highly compatible with organic solvent–based clearing methods. uDISCO is specifically optimized for large, lipid-rich CNS tissues (e.g., intact spinal cord >2 cm and whole-brain regions) and provides strong delipidation, high refractive index (RI) matching, and excellent preservation of DiI/DiD fluorescence—unlike aqueous methods that suffer from poor dye retention or slow penetration. uDISCO also enables uniform clearing across heterogeneous tissue densities (spinal cord white matter vs. thalamic nuclei vs. cortical layers) and supports 3D reconstruction of long projections without signal quenching. Critically, it avoids antibody-based labeling (which was misapplied in the original protocol) and directly leverages the pre-existing DiI/DiD tracers as the sole fluorescent reporters, satisfying the constraint of using only listed dyes and no extraneous fluorophores.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation

2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

3.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) methanol : DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

4.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) BABB (1:2).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Final Mounting and Storage

**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The sample is lipid-rich scWAT requiring strong delipidation and high refractive index (RI) matching for deep imaging of fine neural structures. uDISCO is a solvent-based method established for T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tissues, offering rapid, high-clearing power with excellent antibody penetration and compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes. PGP9.5 and CGRP are validated target-specific markers for sensory nerve fibers in white adipose tissue; co-staining provides robust and specific labeling of the required target. DAPI is omitted due to marker-level cautions against nuclear counterstains for PGP9.5 and because it is not target-specific. Endogenous FPs are avoided per protocol constraints; all labeling uses antibody-conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes compatible with uDISCO.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for lipid-rich tissue with potential heme pigments)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)

6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, total washing time: 6 hours  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining

8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 four times, total washing time: 5 hours  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 647, anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method with high delipidation power and strong compatibility with exogenous fluorescent labels, making it ideal for lipid-rich tissues like scWAT (T10_LIPID_OR_PIGMENT_RICH tier). It enables deep antibody penetration into dense, thick samples (~1 cm³) and achieves robust transparency within several days. Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses target-specific primary antibodies—CGRP for peptidergic sensory fibers and PGP9.5 as a validated pan-neuronal marker for sensory nerve fibers in adipose tissue—conjugated via secondary antibodies to Alexa Fluor dyes fully compatible with FDISCO. Lectin/IB4 was removed due to marker-level cautions against its use with PGP9.5 and to maintain strict target specificity. This refined combination allows precise 3D mapping of CGRP⁺ sensory fibers relative to total nerves (PGP9.5), fulfilling the spatial relationship goals without incompatible reagents.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for lipid-rich tissue with residual heme)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing: rabbit anti-CGRP (1:200) and mouse anti-PGP9.5 (1:500). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washes Post Primary Staining  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat 6.1 two more times with fresh solution each time. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Washes Post Secondary Staining  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat 8.1 two more times with fresh solution each time. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat 10.2 once with fresh DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 ratio). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh BABB (1:2). (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage)  
12.2 Mount in BABB-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional RI adjustment.

It preserves tissue morphology with minimal distortion while enabling robust immunolabeling in dense white adipose tissue (WAT). Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in solvent-based methods, so target-specific immunolabeling is essential. CGRP is the canonical marker for peptidergic sensory nerve fibers in adipose tissue; PGP9.5 (UCHL1) serves as a pan-neuronal marker to delineate the total innervation network—both are valid target-specific markers per the labeling requirements. Lectin (IB4) was removed because it is not a target-specific marker for sensory nerve fibers and is cautioned against when used with PGP9.5. Alexa Fluor 568 and Alexa Fluor 647 are fully compatible with FDISCO and provide spectrally separable channels for precise 3D mapping of sensory versus total nerve fibers across adipose microdomains (central, perivascular, septal, marginal).

**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense mineralized hard tissues like bone (T07 tier), enabling deep antibody penetration and efficient lipid removal while preserving dye-based fluorescence. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes and lectins, and effectively clears both cranial and long bones. PGP9.5 and β-III Tubulin are target-specific pan-neuronal markers essential for mapping the bone tissue sensory and general neural networks as required; IB4 lectin labels sensory nerve endings in bone marrow and perivascular regions, providing complementary target-specific labeling. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific and are explicitly cautioned against for PGP9.5 and β-III Tubulin per marker-level compatibility guidance. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched by FDISCO, so dye-conjugated antibodies/lectins are required—this aligns with the problem’s need for specific, identity-resolving neural labeling beyond mere path tracing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

4.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-PGP9.5 (1:200), anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500), and biotinylated IB4 lectin (10 µg/mL), all diluted in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100 and 5% normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically established for dense mineralized tissues like bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), enabling deep antibody penetration into cranial and femoral bone while preserving fine neural morphology with minimal distortion relative to other organic solvent methods. It efficiently clears both cortical bone and marrow-containing cavities, critical for visualizing intraosseous nerve networks. Since endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in FDISCO, we use immunolabeling: CGRP is the gold-standard marker for peptidergic sensory nerve fibers in bone; PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) labels the broader neural network; IB4-Lectin highlights non-peptidergic sensory fibers and vascular endothelium as an auxiliary channel. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific and are explicitly cautioned against for PGP9.5 per marker-level compatibility guidance. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568/647) are validated as FDISCO-compatible and do not violate any marker-fluorophore restrictions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rabbit anti-CGRP (1:200), mouse anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), and biotinylated IB4 (10 µg/mL) in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500), donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), and streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer samples to glass vials filled with fresh DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage at RT in dark)  
5.2 Mount in DBE-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)
