**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 568, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for mineralized hard tissues (e.g., bone) and provides deep antibody penetration while preserving far-red fluorophores like Alexa Fluor 568/647. Unlike BoneClear, FDISCO includes optimized delipidation and decalcification-compatible steps that enhance transparency in dense bone without excessive antigen damage. The labeling strategy uses two target-specific neural markers: CGRP for peptidergic sensory fibers and PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) to visualize the full neural network in bone, marrow, and meninges. Both are compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent workflow and avoid nuclear counterstains that interfere with bone autofluorescence or mask fine axonal structures.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Rehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days; change solution every 2 days)  
1.2 Wash with PBS three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  
1.3 Gradual rehydration: incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500) and anti-PGP9.5 (1:1000) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days; gentle agitation)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Wash with PBST (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS) six times. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days; protected from light)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBST six times. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Repeat 100% methanol incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation and Bleaching  
8.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours; protected from light)  
8.2 Wash with 100% methanol twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

9 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.5 Final incubation with fresh ethyl cinnamate for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour; store at RT in dark until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for hard tissues (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), providing strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for dense, mineralized samples like bone. It enables deep antibody penetration required for visualizing bone marrow sympathetic nerve fibers and hematopoietic niche components. Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is fully compatible with synthetic dyes such as Alexa Fluor 488 and 568. TH and NPY are validated target-specific markers for catecholaminergic and peptidergic sympathetic nerve terminals in the bone marrow microenvironment, respectively, and their dual labeling with spectrally distinct, photostable Alexa Fluor conjugates allows precise spatial mapping within the hematopoietic niche without reliance on nuclear counterstains or pan-lineage markers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution, pH 7.4, supplemented with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days with gentle agitation; change solution every 3 days)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-NPY (1:200) diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 4 changes)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:300) in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 4 changes)  

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)  

8 Delipidation and Clearing  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)  
8.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

9.1 Incubation with FDISCO RI-matching solution (ethyl cinnamate : dibenzyl ether = 1:1, RI ≈ 1.56) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense mineralized tissues like bone and compatible with thick composite samples (cranial bone, femur, meninges, marrow). It enables deep antibody and dye penetration while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes (Alexa Fluor series) and lectins—critical for labeling CGRP⁺ sensory fibers (target-specific), pan-neuronal PGP9.5, and vascular lumen via IB4/Lectin. Endogenous FPs are quenched, but this is irrelevant as all targets require immunostaining or exogenous labeling. FDISCO’s speed and strong delipidation/clearing capacity suit the high difficulty of bone-marrow-meninges complexes, and its RI-matching solvents support high-resolution light-sheet imaging of 3D neurovascular trajectories through bone channels.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Mild Decalcification (pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution, pH 7.4, with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days; change solution every 2 days)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Rehydration: reverse methanol series (80% → 60% → 40% → 20% in PBS, 30 min each). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
2.7 Incubation with blocking buffer: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody and Lectin Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:200), anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), and biotinylated IB4 (1:100) in antibody dilution buffer (1% NDS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Streptavidin Conjugate Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), and streptavidin–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-labeling Washes  
6.1 Wash with PBST, 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

7 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation with fresh solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Delipidation and Bleaching  
8.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

9 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi for final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Store samples in glass vials filled with ECi at RT in the dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite until imaging)  
10.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional steps. (Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense mineralized tissues like mouse long bones and skull, enabling deep antibody penetration into enclosed bone marrow cavities. It preserves fluorescence of synthetic dyes (Alexa Fluor series) but quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins—thus requiring immunolabeling. TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) is the canonical marker for catecholaminergic sympathetic nerve fibers, while NPY (neuropeptide Y) labels peptidergic sympathetic terminals; co-staining allows direct comparison of the two sympathetic subtypes. CD31 labels bone marrow vasculature for spatial reference to vascular niches within the hematopoietic stem cell microenvironment. DAPI was removed as it is a nuclear counterstain and not a target-specific marker for either bone marrow sympathetic nerve endings or the hematopoietic stem cell niche, per labeling requirements. FDISCO’s strong delipidation and compatibility with pre-decalcification ensure minimal light scattering in bone while maintaining 3D morphology suitable for quantitative morphometry of nerve density, branching, and spatial relationships.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-Clearing Decalcification (required for dense murine bone)  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4, with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

2 Immunolabeling (performed before organic dehydration to preserve epitopes)  
2.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Primary antibody incubation: anti-TH (1:200), anti-NPY (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:100) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  
2.4 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 4 changes)  
2.5 Secondary antibody incubation: Alexa Fluor 488–donkey anti-rabbit (1:300), Alexa Fluor 568–donkey anti-guinea pig (1:300), Alexa Fluor 647–donkey anti-rat (1:300) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
2.6 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 4 changes)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

4 Delipidation and Bleaching  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours in dark)  
4.2 Wash with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 changes)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 changes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 ratio). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.4 Final incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with DBE for long-term storage at RT in dark. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
6.2 Mount in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically established for dense hard tissues like bone and bone marrow (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA tier). It enables deep antibody penetration into mineralized bone while preserving fine neural structures. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses target-specific primary antibodies against TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, marker of noradrenergic sympathetic nerve terminals) and NPY (neuropeptide Y, marker of peptidergic sympathetic fibers), combined with CD31 to label vascular endothelium for spatial reference—ensuring specific identification of sympathetic innervation relative to bone marrow niches. All chosen Alexa Fluor dyes are compatible with FDISCO per compatibility data. FDISCO’s strong delipidation and decalcification-like action (via organic solvents) effectively clears calcified bone without requiring separate decalcification, preserving 3D architecture of marrow cavities.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200), anti-NPY (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:100) in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, total washing time: 6 hours  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit (1:400), Alexa Fluor 568 anti-guinea pig (1:400), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rat (1:400) in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, total washing time: 6 hours  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh BABB (1:2).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer samples to glass vials filled with BABB (1:2) and store at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite until imaging)  
12.2 Mount samples in BABB-compatible imaging chambers for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional RI adjustment.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for mineralized hard tissues like mouse bone (femur, tibia, skull), enabling deep antibody and dye penetration into dense bone marrow cavities. It preserves synthetic fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series) while efficiently removing lipids and matching refractive index for high-resolution 3D imaging. The chosen labeling strategy directly targets the scientific goals: TH immunostaining identifies catecholaminergic sympathetic nerve fibers, and NPY immunostaining identifies peptidergic sympathetic nerve fibers—both are target-specific markers for 骨髓交感神经末梢. Lectin (Isolectin B4) was removed because it is not a target-specific marker for either 骨髓交感神经末梢 or 造血干细胞微环境 per domain guidance, and its use with NPY/Osx-class targets is cautioned against. All remaining fluorophores are compatible with FDISCO per domain knowledge.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone marrow autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-TH (1:200) and anti-NPY (1:200) diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-guinea pig IgG (1:400) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) NDS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage or immediate imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Mount cleared bones in glass-bottom imaging chambers filled with DBE, orienting regions of interest (e.g., metaphysis, endosteal surface) toward objective.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (灌注血管腔面标记) + CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647 (血管内皮结构)]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires simultaneous visualization of functional perfused vasculature (via intravascular Lectin labeling) and total vascular endothelial architecture (via CD31 immunostaining) in a dense, fixed glioma tissue block (~8 mm scale). FDISCO is selected because it offers strong delipidation and high refractive index matching for large, lipid-rich brain tumor samples, preserves exogenous fluorophores including Alexa Fluor dyes and Lectin conjugates (unlike iDISCO+ which quenches them), and enables deep antibody penetration. Lectin (e.g., DyLight 594- or 647-conjugated) injected pre-fixation labels only perfused vessels, while post-fixation anti-CD31 staining reveals the full endothelial network—including non-perfused, abnormal segments—allowing quantitative comparison of perfusion fraction, vessel continuity, and normalization metrics. FDISCO’s compatibility with both Lectin and Alexa Fluor 647 ensures signal retention through dehydration and clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigment present)  
2.1 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (anti-CD31)  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody diluted 1:200 in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 five times, changing solution every 1 hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 diluted 1:500 in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 five times, changing solution every 1 hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with ethyl cinnamate (ECi) and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for high refractive index matching, strong delipidation, and excellent preservation of exogenous fluorophores—including Alexa Fluor dyes and lectin conjugates—while enabling deep penetration into dense, fixed tumor tissue (~8 mm scale). It is established for whole mouse brain and tumor blocks, provides minimal fluorescence quenching for Alexa Fluor 488/647, and supports high-resolution imaging of both structural (CD31) and functional perfusion (intravascular lectin) vasculature. Lectin injected intravenously prior to fixation labels only perfused (functional) vessels, while anti-CD31 immunostaining reveals total endothelial architecture. FDISCO’s compatibility with both probes allows direct spatial comparison of perfused vs. structural vasculature in the same sample—critical for assessing vascular normalization post anti-angiogenic therapy.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Pre-labeling (Performed prior to fixation; assumed completed but specified for completeness)  
1.1 Intracardiac perfusion with PBS followed by injection of fluorescently conjugated Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum lectin, 1 mg/mL in PBS) via tail vein or left ventricle 10 min before sacrifice to label functional, perfused vasculature. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes circulation)  

2 Fixation  
2.1 Post-perfusion fixation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Wash in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

4 Immunostaining for CD31  
4.1 Incubation in blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM1), 1:200 dilution in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
4.3 Wash in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 6 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500 dilution in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.5 Wash in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 6 hours)  

5 Dehydration  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

6 Delipidation and Bleaching  
6.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Rehydration (for optional post-clearing nuclear counterstain if needed; omitted here per problem focus)  

8 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Final RI Matching and Storage  
9.1 Transfer to fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi in glass vial, sealed to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging; stable for weeks at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample contains endogenous tdTomato/RFP signal in breast cancer cells, which must be preserved for 3D mapping of metastatic foci. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method established for whole mouse brain (5–12 mm scale), fully compatible with tdTomato fluorescence, supports deep antibody penetration, and minimizes tissue distortion—critical for accurate morphometric analysis of invasion patterns. To confirm epithelial identity of metastatic cells and distinguish them from autofluorescent background or non-specific signals, we add immunostaining against Pan-Cytokeratin (a pan-epithelial marker highly specific for carcinoma cells) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, which is compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from tdTomato.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash tissue 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (e.g., clone AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 2 hours in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.6 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 2 hours in PBST, then 2 × 1 hour in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: as indicated)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40).(Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer cleared brain into fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)  
3.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in MACS-R2 at RT for ≥2 hours to minimize thermal drift during light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The problem requires preservation of endogenous tdTomato/RFP signal and specific identification of epithelial-derived metastatic carcinoma cells via Pan-Cytokeratin, while maintaining low tissue distortion in a dense, lipid-rich whole mouse brain (~12 mm). Solvent-based methods (e.g., uDISCO, iDISCO+) were previously used with high voltage electrophoretic delipidation, causing structural damage and weak reference signals—likely due to FP quenching and excessive shrinkage. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method established for whole mouse brains in the T04 tier, fully compatible with tdTomato and Alexa Fluor 568, supports deep antibody penetration without electrophoresis, and minimizes morphological distortion. Pan-Cytokeratin is a validated target-specific marker for epithelial cancer cell remnants in metastasis contexts and pairs optimally with Alexa Fluor 568 under MACS conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (mouse or rabbit monoclonal, 1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours, change buffer daily)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:500 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours, change buffer daily)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue into final RI-matching solution: MACS-R2 (same as 2.3) in glass vial (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours before imaging)  
3.2 Store long-term in MACS-R2 at 4 ℃ in the dark; image within 4 weeks for optimal tdTomato and Alexa Fluor 568 signal integrity.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato/RFP (endogenous), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous tdTomato/RFP signal from metastatic breast cancer cells, deep penetration of immunolabeling for epithelial identity (Pan-Cytokeratin), and visualization of vasculature (Lectin/IB4) to assess perivascular invasion. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that preserves fluorescent protein signals, supports robust antibody and lectin penetration in whole mouse brains (~1 cm scale), and is compatible with all selected fluorophores (tdTomato, Alexa Fluor 647/488). Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), MACS avoids quenching of endogenous RFP and minimizes tissue distortion—critical for accurate 3D mapping of tumor–brain interface architecture. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific markers and are cautioned against when used with Pan-Cytokeratin or Lectin per marker-level compatibility guidance.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary reagents: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:200) and biotinylated IB4 lectin (10 µg/mL) in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary reagents: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated streptavidin (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue into fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage or immediate imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
3.2 Prior to light-sheet or confocal imaging, equilibrate sample in MACS-R2 at RT for at least 2 hours to ensure optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (内源), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous tdTomato/RFP fluorescence from breast cancer cells while enabling specific immunodetection of epithelial identity via an epithelial marker. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that robustly preserves fluorescent proteins (including tdTomato/RFP) and supports deep antibody penetration in dense tissues like adult mouse brain containing metastases. Among compatible epithelial markers, Pan-Cytokeratin is a well-established pan-epithelial cytokeratin marker that specifically labels carcinoma cells of epithelial origin and is distinct from brain parenchymal elements. Conjugation to Alexa Fluor 647 ensures spectral separation from tdTomato (emission ~580–620 nm) and compatibility with MACS. Solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) were excluded due to risk of FP quenching despite some being listed as “FP-compatible” under specific conditions; MACS provides consistent FP retention with lower tissue distortion—critical for spatial analysis of micro-metastases.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Immunostaining for Epithelial Identity  
2.1 Blocking with Blocking Buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (e.g., clone AE1/AE3, 1:200 dilution) in Antibody Dilution Buffer (1% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle agitation)  
2.3 Washing with PBST (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes, total 18 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300 dilution) in Antibody Dilution Buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  
2.5 Washing with PBST (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes, total 18 hours)  

3 Optical Clearing with MACS  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
4.1 Transfer sample into imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
4.2 Store at 4 ℃ in MACS-R2 if not imaged immediately (protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-TH + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically established for mineralized hard tissues like mouse bone (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep antibody penetration into dense, lipid-rich, and calcified matrices after appropriate decalcification and delipidation, which is essential for visualizing fine neural fibers throughout the intact femur. Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor–conjugated antibodies. The chosen markers—CGRP for peptidergic nociceptive sensory fibers and TH for sympathetic fibers—are target-specific, validated in bone pain models, and distinguishable via spectrally separated fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488 and 568). DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific and are cautioned against for TH. This combination allows precise 3D mapping of both neural populations in bone marrow, endosteum, periosteum, tumor niches, and perivascular zones without relying on non-specific tracers or incompatible counterstains.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution, pH 7.4, with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Permeabilization  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Repeat wash with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Immunolabeling  
5.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rabbit anti-CGRP (1:200) and goat anti-TH (1:200) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  
5.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  
5.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking)  
5.5 Wash with PBST, 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

6 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.5 Transfer to fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for storage and imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, it is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor–conjugated antibodies and nuclear counterstains like DAPI. The chosen markers—CGRP for peptidergic nociceptive sensory fibers and TH for sympathetic fibers—are target-specific, validated in bone pain models, and distinguishable via spectrally separated fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488 and 568). This combination allows precise 3D mapping of both neural populations in bone marrow, endosteum, periosteum, tumor niches, and perivascular zones without relying on non-specific tracers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution, pH 7.4, with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days)  

2 Dehydration

2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rabbit anti-CGRP (1:200) and goat anti-TH (1:200) in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  
5.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  
5.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in blocking buffer, plus DAPI (1:1000). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking)

6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse or anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:400 in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 568, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense mineralized tissues like bone (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep antibody penetration into intact mouse femur while preserving fine neural morphology with minimal autofluorescence—critical for resolving CGRP⁺ sensory fibers within the complex bone microenvironment. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling relies on exogenous immunostaining and lectin probes, which are fully compatible. CGRP is the canonical marker for peptidergic nociceptive fibers in bone; PGP9.5 (UCHL1) serves as a pan-neuronal marker to delineate the total intraosseous nerve network; IB4 (isolectin B4 from Griffonia simplicifolia) labels non-peptidergic sensory fibers and vasculature-associated structures, providing complementary spatial reference for vascular niches. All three primary labels are conjugated to Alexa Fluor dyes (568, 647, 488), which are explicitly compatible with FDISCO per the knowledge base.  

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Decalcification Pre-treatment  
2.1 Incubation with 5% (wt/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 30% (wt/vol) ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA), pH 7.4, in PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation and daily EDTA replacement)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Rehydration through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
3.2 Permeabilization and blocking: incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, and 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Primary antibody incubation: anti-CGRP (1:200) and anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  
3.4 Washing: PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 3 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  
3.5 Secondary antibody and lectin co-staining: Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated IB4 (10 μg/mL) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light)  
3.6 Final wash: PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 3 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

4 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Organic Solvent Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer cleared femur into glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with DBE, orienting longitudinal axis for optimal light-sheet or confocal z-stack acquisition.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 568, TH + Alexa Fluor 647, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense mineralized tissues like mouse long bones (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep antibody penetration into bone marrow cavities and preserves fine neural morphology with minimal background—critical for resolving CGRP⁺ sensory and TH⁺ sympathetic nerve fibers in 3D. Unlike BoneClear without decalcification, FDISCO incorporates an EDTA-based decalcification step that is compatible with protein epitopes when performed under cold, neutral pH conditions, thereby rescuing weak immunosignal observed previously. The chosen labeling strategy uses three target-specific primary antibodies (CGRP for peptidergic nociceptors, TH for sympathetic fibers, PGP9.5 as a pan-neuronal marker) conjugated to spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes—all confirmed compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent environment and resistant to quenching. This triplex labeling allows direct comparison of nerve subtypes across bone compartments (periosteum, endosteum, marrow, tumor niche) without relying on endogenous fluorescence.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4, adjusted with NaOH) in PBS containing 0.1% NaN₃. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with daily solution change)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Permeabilization  
3.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Rehydration (for antibody labeling)  
4.1 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.6 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Immunolabeling  
5.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% normal donkey serum + 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500), anti-TH (1:500), anti-PGP9.5 (1:1000) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  
5.3 Wash with PBT (6 changes over 2 days, 4 hours per wash). (Temperature: RT, Time: total 48 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 568 donkey anti-rabbit (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti-mouse (1:500), Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-goat (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days, with gentle agitation)  
5.5 Wash with PBT (6 changes over 2 days, 4 hours per wash). (Temperature: RT, Time: total 48 hours)  

6 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) DCM : ethyl cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% ECi. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.3 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% ECi. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh 100% ECi and seal. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage; image within 2 weeks for optimal signal)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-TH + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + DyLight 594]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense mineralized hard tissues like mouse long bones (tier T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep penetration of antibodies and lectins into intact femurs while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes (Alexa Fluor series, DyLight, IB4/Lectin). Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy relies entirely on exogenous immunostaining and lectin perfusion-compatible dyes, which are fully compatible with FDISCO. The method achieves rapid, high-fidelity clearing of ~15 mm bone samples with minimal light scattering, enabling high-resolution 3D mapping of CGRP⁺ sensory fibers, TH⁺ sympathetic fibers, PGP9.5⁺ pan-neuronal processes, and IB4⁺ vascular lumens in the tumor-bone microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (wt/vol) BSA + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-CGRP (1:200), anti-TH (1:200), anti-PGP9.5 (1:200), and biotinylated IB4 (10 µg/mL) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing PBT every 2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: total 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Visualization  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:200), Alexa Fluor 568 donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:200), Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti-chicken IgG (1:200), and DyLight 594-conjugated streptavidin (1:200) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, changing PBT every 2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: total 12 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

11 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi and seal with parafilm.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage or immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of endogenous tdTomato fluorescence from Wnt1-Cre;tdTomato reporter mice and robust immunodetection of the nuclear transcription factor Sox10 in a small (~5 mm) fixed embryonic trunk. Ce3D is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method established for T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM tissues that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including tdTomato), enables deep antibody penetration into dense embryonic tissue, and minimizes morphological distortion—critical for accurate spatial mapping of migrating neural crest cells. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), Ce3D does not quench FP signals. Alexa Fluor 647 was selected for Sox10 due to its photostability, far-red emission (minimal spectral overlap with tdTomato), and compatibility with Ce3D.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (perform before clearing to ensure antibody penetration)  
1.1 Wash fixed embryo trunks in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 changes)  
1.2 Incubation in blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Sox10 (e.g., R&D Systems AF2864 or equivalent), diluted 1:200 in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.4 Wash in PBT (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 5 changes, total 10 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-goat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:500 in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.6 Wash in PBT (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 5 changes, total 10 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with Ce3D  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 15% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B (50% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-M (88% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Transfer sample to fresh Ce3D-M in imaging chamber (glass-bottom dish or capillary) (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Store cleared samples immersed in Ce3D-M at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 2 weeks without signal degradation  
4.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with excitation/emission settings: tdTomato (Ex/Em ≈ 554/581 nm), Alexa Fluor 647 (Ex/Em ≈ 650/668 nm)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method specifically validated for small whole embryonic tissues (1–5 mm) that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins like tdTomato without quenching, enables deep antibody penetration for nuclear transcription factors such as Sox10, and minimizes tissue distortion—critical for reconstructing precise 3D migration paths of neural crest cells. Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), Ce3D avoids methanol dehydration and harsh decolorization steps that degraded tdTomato signal and disrupted morphology in the prior ClearT2 attempt. Alexa Fluor 568 is compatible with Ce3D and spectrally separable from tdTomato, allowing dual-channel imaging of lineage (tdTomato+) and glial/neural crest identity (Sox10+).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (performed before clearing to ensure antibody access)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Sox10 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 4 changes, 2 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A (25% (wt/vol) N-methyldiethanolamine, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-B (25% (wt/vol) N-methyldiethanolamine, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-C (25% (wt/vol) N-methyldiethanolamine, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-M (final RI matching solution: 30% (wt/vol) N-methyldiethanolamine, 35% (wt/vol) urea, 40% (vol/vol) glycerol in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with fresh Ce3D-M for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (store at 4 ℃ in dark if not imaged immediately; stable for ≥2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample is a small (1–5 mm), fixed mouse embryonic trunk at E9.5–E10.5 expressing endogenous tdTomato under Wnt1-Cre, requiring preservation of this red fluorescent protein signal. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that robustly preserves tdTomato fluorescence while enabling deep antibody penetration for target-specific markers like Sox10. It avoids organic solvents that quench FPs (e.g., uDISCO/iDISCO+) and offers faster clearing than CUBIC or ScaleS for small embryonic tissues. DAPI was removed from labeling because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific and marker-level cautions advise against DAPI when using Sox10.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (performed before clearing to ensure antibody penetration)  
1.1 Wash samples 3 × 1 hour in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.2 Block in blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody: anti-Sox10 (e.g., R&D Systems MAB2864 or equivalent) diluted 1:200 in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash 5 × 2 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:400 in blocking buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.6 Wash 5 × 2 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with MACS  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Transfer samples to fresh MACS-R2 and store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite for short-term storage <1 month)  
3.2 Mount samples in glass-bottom dishes or capillaries filled with MACS-R2 for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-PSD95 + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-Homer1 + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-fidelity 3D visualization of two excitatory postsynaptic scaffold proteins (PSD95 and Homer1) alongside dendritic architecture in thick (1–2 mm) fixed mouse hippocampal CA1 tissue. Ce3D is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method established for thick brain slices (T02 tier), offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology with minimal shrinkage—critical for spatial analysis of puncta distribution across CA1 strata. It supports deep penetration of antibodies and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes (488/568/647), enabling robust multiplexed immunolabeling. PSD95 and Homer1 are target-specific markers for excitatory postsynaptic structures; MAP2 is a validated structural marker for CA1 dendrites and dendritic spines, providing essential morphological context without substituting for functional synaptic labeling. Nuclear dyes are omitted per constraints, as they do not substitute for target-specific labeling.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.1 M PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (0.1 M PBS, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution: anti-PSD95 (1:200), anti-Homer1 (1:200), anti-MAP2 (1:500).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Wash with 0.1 M PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

5 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (anti-mouse, 1:400), Alexa Fluor 568 (anti-rabbit, 1:400), and Alexa Fluor 647 (anti-chicken or appropriate host for MAP2, 1:400) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Post-labeling Wash  
6.1 Wash with 0.1 M PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, with 4 buffer changes)  

7 Clearing with Ce3D Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution A (8.5% (wt/vol) sorbitol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution B (25% (wt/vol) sorbitol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Matching Solution (80% (wt/vol) sorbitol in 0.1 M PBS, pH adjusted to 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer samples to fresh Ce3D-Matching Solution in imaging-compatible glass-bottom dishes or chambers.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: until imaging; stable for ≥1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for high-lipid, pigment-rich tissues like placenta, offering strong delipidation and hemoglobin removal while preserving exogenous fluorophores such as Alexa Fluor dyes and lectins. It effectively reduces blood-derived background autofluorescence and enables deep penetration of antibodies and lectins into dense vascular networks. Lectin (IB4) specifically labels functional perfused vasculature lumens via endothelial glycocalyx binding, while anti-CD31 immunostaining reveals total endothelial cell morphology—enabling dual visualization of structural vasculature and perfused compartments. FDISCO is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 568 and 647, and supports low-background 3D imaging of complex microvascular trees in thick samples.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Hemoglobin Bleaching  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Rehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Blocking and Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution: PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rat anti-CD31 (PECAM1, 1:200) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 three more times (total 4 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Co-staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and biotinylated IB4 lectin (10 μg/mL), both diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Post-staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 three more times (total 4 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Repeat step 7.4 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.4 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372) for RI matching.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to fresh ECi in glass-bottom imaging dish.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark for up to 1 week)
