**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFAP + Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires high-resolution 3D discrimination of reactive vs. quiescent astrocytes and their spatial relationship to regenerating axons across a large (40 mm), dense spinal cord segment. GFAP is the canonical marker for reactive astrocytes and enables visualization of glial scar morphology; β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) robustly labels all axons, including regenerating fibers, allowing assessment of axonal penetration through or around the scar. iDISCO+ is selected because it is established for long CNS tissues (T06 tier), provides strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration in dense tissue, and is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 conjugates—both critical for multiplexed imaging. Although iDISCO+ quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling relies on exogenous antibody-dye conjugates, which are fully compatible. The method achieves high clearing power with manageable shrinkage, preserving spatial relationships essential for boundary and continuity analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Storage  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) overnight.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.3 Store in PBS at 4 ℃ until processing (max 1 week).  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Bleaching (optional but recommended for spinal cord pigmentation)  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Permeabilization and Blocking  
5.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with blocking solution (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Primary Antibody Staining  
6.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-GFAP (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) (1:500) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  

7 Washes After Primary Antibody  
7.1 Wash with wash buffer (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) six times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

8 Secondary Antibody Staining  
8.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  

9 Washes After Secondary Antibody  
9.1 Wash with wash buffer (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) six times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
9.2 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
12.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

13 Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for light-sheet or confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or store at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9 Post-staining Washes  
9.1 Wash with PBST six times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours per wash, total 36 hours)  
9.2 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Repeat incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

13.1 Image immediately using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filters for Alexa Fluor 488 (ex/em ~495/519 nm) and Alexa Fluor 647 (ex/em ~650/668 nm).  
13.2 For storage, keep samples immersed in DBE at RT in the dark; stable for ≥1 month.

**Justification:** uDISCO is a high-refractive-index solvent-based clearing method established for dense, lipid- and pigment-rich mouse organs (e.g., whole heart), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for visualizing intrinsic cardiac neurons embedded in thick myocardium. **Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-ChAT + Alexa Fluor 488, anti-TH + Alexa Fluor 568, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is an established solvent-based clearing method for dense mouse soft organs (5–20 mm), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration—critical for visualizing sparse cardiac innervation throughout the intact heart. It is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes (488, 568, 647) and preserves their fluorescence intensity under organic solvents, providing high signal-to-noise for ChAT (cholinergic neurons) and TH (sympathetic fibers). Phalloidin-AF647 labels F-actin in cardiomyocytes, enabling precise anatomical registration of neural structures relative to myocardial architecture. Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, all labeling here is antibody- or dye-based, satisfying this constraint. FDISCO also minimizes tissue distortion compared to other solvent methods, better preserving 3D morphology for quantitative analysis of cardiac neural-cardiomyocyte relationships.

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

6 Washes Post Primary  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash 5 times, changing PBT every 1 hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
6.3 Final extended wash in PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-goat IgG–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500), and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) in PBT + 5% NDS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Washes Post Secondary  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash 5 times, changing PBT every 1 hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
8.3 Final extended wash in PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
12.2 Mount in DBE-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Stabilin-2 + Alexa Fluor 488, Lyve-1 + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a rapid, high-refractive-index solvent-based clearing method compatible with thick (≤3 mm) dense tissues like liver slices, achieving full transparency within ~24 hours. It preserves synthetic fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series) and is compatible with lectin-free immunolabeling—critical since Stabilin-2 and Lyve-1 are LSEC-specific markers requiring antibody-based detection, while CD31 serves as a pan-endothelial reference for portal tracts and large vessels. FDISCO avoids endogenous FP quenching issues irrelevant here (no GFP/RFP used) and supports deep antibody penetration in fixed tissue. The chosen triple-labeling strategy enables discrimination of LSEC subtypes (Stabilin-2⁺/Lyve-1⁺) from general vasculature (CD31⁺), fulfilling spatial mapping goals at the lobule scale.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for fixation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Stabilin-2 (1:200), anti-Lyve-1 (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:100) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with species-matched secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 (anti-rat, 1:400), Alexa Fluor 568 (anti-hamster, 1:400), Alexa Fluor 647 (anti-rat, 1:400) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  

6 Rehydration (for RI matching transition)  
6.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with FDISCO-RI matching solution (dibenzyl ether : benzyl alcohol = 1:2, v/v).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount sample in glass-bottom dish filled with FDISCO-RI matching solution for immediate confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: proceed to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-ChAT + Alexa Fluor 568, anti-TH + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method with high delipidation power and excellent deep antibody/dye penetration, ideal for dense, lipid-rich tissues like the intact mouse heart (~10 mm scale). It effectively clears whole organs within several days while preserving signal from robust synthetic fluorophores (Alexa Fluor dyes), which are fully compatible per the knowledge base. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched, so all targets must be labeled via immunostaining or chemical dyes—this aligns with the requirement to detect ChAT (for cholinergic ICN neurons), TH (for noradrenergic sympathetic fibers), and Phalloidin (for F-actin in cardiomyocytes to reveal fiber orientation). DAPI was removed because it is not target-specific and is cautioned against for TH labeling. FDISCO’s strong refractive index matching and full compatibility with all chosen fluorophores enable high-resolution light-sheet imaging of neural-cardiac spatial relationships throughout the entire heart.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for endogenous pigment reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

4.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

6 Washing

8 Post-staining Washes

8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five more times (total 6 washes over 24 hours).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for high-resolution 3D imaging of dense tissues like kidney cortex, offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration while preserving Alexa Fluor dye signals. It is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 488 and 568, which are ideal for labeling the two key slit diaphragm proteins Nephrin and Podocin—core structural components of the glomerular filtration barrier. The 500 μm thickness falls within FDISCO’s optimal range for rapid, uniform clearing without excessive distortion, and its organic solvent system ensures high refractive index matching for light-sheet or confocal imaging with high signal-to-noise ratio.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with anti-Nephrin (NPHS1) antibody (1:200) and anti-Podocin (NPHS2) antibody (1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  

3 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in blocking solution (protected from light).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
5.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer tissue into fresh ECi in glass-bottom imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for up to 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The tissue is a dense, fixed human cortical block requiring deep antibody penetration and minimal morphological distortion. MACS is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK that preserves tissue geometry, supports robust antibody penetration in thick samples, and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes and pan-neuronal structural markers NeuN (nuclear) and MAP2 (dendritic/somatic). Unlike solvent-based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), MACS avoids significant shrinkage and preserves fine cytoarchitecture critical for clinical morphology, while enabling dual-color labeling of mature neuron somata at ~2 mm depth.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-NeuN (1:500) and rabbit anti-MAP2 (1:500) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle agitation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:800) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:800) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
1.5 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle agitation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  

2 Dehydration (optional pre-clearing equilibration for aqueous methods)  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Rehydration through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  

3 Optical Clearing with MACS  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Transfer sample into imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for final RI matching.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour prior to imaging)  
4.2 Mount tissue in glass-bottom dish or capillary compatible with light-sheet microscopy, fully immersed in MACS-R2, sealed to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage up to 1 week at 4 ℃ in dark)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3 + Alexa Fluor 488, CD8 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for dense, lipid-rich FFPE-derived thick tissue slices (≤500 μm), offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching while preserving exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor dyes. It enables deep antibody penetration required for immunostaining in thick tumor sections and minimizes fluorescence quenching compared to other organic solvent methods. The dual-marker strategy uses CD3 as a pan-T cell marker and CD8 to specifically identify cytotoxic T cell subsets—both are well-validated, target-specific markers for tumor-infiltrating T cells in human FFPE tumor pathology. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are highly compatible with FDISCO, providing bright, photostable signals with minimal bleed-through for multiplexed 3D imaging. Nuclear counterstains (e.g., DAPI) are avoided per compatibility cautions for CD3/CD8 labeling in solvent-based protocols.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Rehydrate tissue through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each at RT.  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CD3 (1:200) and anti-CD8 (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.4 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

3 Secondary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with PBST, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each, protected from light)  

4 Dehydration (post-staining)  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation and Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
5.2 Wash with 100% methanol, 2 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  

6 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer tissue into fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate in a glass-bottom imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes before imaging)  
7.2 Seal chamber to prevent ECi evaporation and proceed to confocal or light-sheet microscopy within 24 hours.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based high-refractive-index clearing method established for dense tissues like mouse heart (T02_THICK_SLICE_0P5_3MM), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration while preserving fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes. It is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 568 and 647, enabling robust dual-labeling of α-SMA (a specific marker for activated myofibroblasts in fibrotic regions) and CD31 (a canonical endothelial marker for coronary vasculature). This combination allows simultaneous 3D visualization of myofibroblast-enriched fibrotic zones and the coronary vascular tree with minimal signal quenching, critical for resolving spatial relationships between extracellular matrix remodeling and vascular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 changes)  
1.3 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Rehydrate tissue through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 1 hour each at RT.  
3.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-α-SMA (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
3.4 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

4 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
4.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

5 Dehydration (Post-Labeling)  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

6 Delipidation and Bleaching  
6.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 changes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
7.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 changes)  
7.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer tissue into fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi in imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for thick tissue slices (0.5–3 mm), offering excellent preservation of lung alveolar architecture with minimal distortion—critical for visualizing delicate air sacs. It supports deep penetration of both lectin and antibody labels while preserving fluorescence from Alexa Fluor dyes. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) binds specifically to glycoproteins on the luminal surface of perfused vasculature, enabling functional vascular mapping; CD31 (PECAM1) immunostaining labels endothelial cells throughout the pulmonary vascular network, providing structural context. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific and are explicitly cautioned against for both CD31 and Lectin labeling per marker-level compatibility guidance. Ce3D’s compatibility with Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647, along with its gentle, non-shrinking protocol, makes it optimal for this application.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Perfusion Labeling  
1.1 Transcardial perfusion of live mouse with ice-cold PBS followed by 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.2 Post-fixation of excised lung lobe in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with fluorescently conjugated Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin-Alexa Fluor 647, 50 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Immunostaining for CD31  
2.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibody anti-CD31 (rat monoclonal, 1:200 dilution) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.4 Washing with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody anti-rat IgG-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 dilution) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.6 Final washes with PBS (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3 Ce3D Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D Reagent A (25% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 15% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with Ce3D Reagent B (50% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Incubation with Ce3D Mounting Solution (88% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.47).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with Ce3D Mounting Solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 488, CD19+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The lymph node is a small (3 mm), dense immune organ requiring strong antibody penetration and minimal structural distortion to resolve B cell follicles and germinal centers. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method established for T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM, offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology, compatibility with Alexa Fluor dyes, and deep antibody penetration without hazardous solvents. B220 (PTPRC) is a pan-B cell marker that robustly outlines B cell follicles, while CD19 provides complementary B cell-specific labeling enriched in germinal centers; both are target-specific and compatible with post-fixation immunostaining. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are highly stable, bright, and fully compatible with MACS, enabling high-contrast dual-channel 3D imaging of follicular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Fixation  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Repeat PBST wash twice.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

3 Permeabilization and Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Primary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with rat anti-mouse B220 (PTPRC) (1:200) and rat anti-mouse CD19 (1:200) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Repeat PBST wash three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

6 Secondary Antibody Staining  
6.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Repeat PBST wash three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

8 Dehydration (Optional pre-clearing equilibration for MACS)  
8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Tissue Optical Clearing  
9.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
9.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

10 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
10.1 Transfer sample to fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage or immediate imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem requires preservation of endogenous tdTomato fluorescence for long-range projection tracing, which excludes solvent-based clearing methods that quench fluorescent proteins (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO). Among FP-compatible aqueous methods established for adult mouse whole brain (T04 tier), MACS offers strong clearing power, deep antibody penetration, minimal distortion, and compatibility with both tdTomato and Alexa Fluor 647. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) is a pan-neuronal axonal marker ideal for visualizing axon scaffold structure and pairs well with far-red Alexa Fluor 647, which is compatible with MACS and minimally overlaps with tdTomato emission.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) diluted 1:500 in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 5 changes over 48 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:300 in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 5 changes over 48 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total, protected from light)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours, gentle agitation)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle agitation)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, gentle agitation)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Equilibration in final imaging medium: MACS-R2 (same as 2.3) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Mount brain in glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh MACS-R2, orient for light-sheet imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 1 week protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD45+Alexa Fluor 647, CD11b+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically established for hard tissues like bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), enabling deep antibody penetration into mineralized and dense samples such as the 1 mm-thick mouse parietal bone with intact marrow cavity. It effectively removes lipids and decalcifies to a degree sufficient for optical access while preserving dye-based fluorescence. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in FDISCO, so we use antibody-conjugated Alexa Fluor dyes: CD45 (pan-immune cell marker) labeled with Alexa Fluor 647 and CD11b (myeloid lineage marker) labeled with Alexa Fluor 488—both compatible with FDISCO per the knowledge base and target-specific for bone marrow immune populations. Nuclear counterstains are avoided per cautions for these targets.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Decalcification (FDISCO-compatible)  
2.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM):methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Immunolabeling (performed after initial dehydration but before final RI matching; rehydration not required due to FDISCO’s organic-phase labeling compatibility)  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-CD45 (1:200) + anti-CD11b (1:200) in FDISCO-Ab buffer (5% DMSO, 0.2% Triton X-100 in methanol).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rat IgG (1:300) + Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) in FDISCO-Ab buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.4 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM):benzyl alcohol (BA).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol (BA).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate (BB).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Final Clearing and Mounting  
5.1 Incubation with FDISCO mounting solution: 1:2 (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, RI ≈ 1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with BABB for light-sheet microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Stabilin-2 + Alexa Fluor 488, Lyve-1 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for dense, lipid-rich whole organs like adult mouse liver (T05_MOUSE_SOFT_ORGAN_5_20MM), offering strong delipidation and deep antibody penetration while preserving fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes. It is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647, which are ideal for dual-target immunolabeling. Stabilin-2 and Lyve-1 are two well-validated, liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC)-specific markers that together comprehensively label the hepatic sinusoidal network—avoiding reliance on pan-endothelial markers like CD31 that may underrepresent LSECs. FDISCO’s high refractive index matching enables optimal light-sheet imaging of the intact vascular topology with minimal signal loss.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Perfuse adult mouse transcardially with ice-cold PBS followed by 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: perfusion until liver appears pale and firm)  
1.2 Dissect whole liver and post-fix in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubate in permeabilization buffer (PBS, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Block in blocking buffer (PBS, 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 5% (wt/vol) BSA).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubate with primary antibodies: rat anti-Stabilin-2 (1:200) and rabbit anti-Lyve-1 (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (PBS, 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 3% (wt/vol) BSA).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Wash thoroughly in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubate with secondary antibodies: goat anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Wash thoroughly in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 12 hours)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation and Bleaching  
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Wash with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer cleared liver to fresh ECi in glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: store indefinitely or proceed immediately to imaging)  
6.2 Mount sample in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet microscope.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for whole-mount embryonic samples (E14 mouse embryo falls within the T03_SMALL_WHOLE_SAMPLE_1_5MM tier), offering high transparency, excellent preservation of exogenous fluorophores (including Alexa Fluor dyes), and compatibility with immunolabeling. It outperforms aqueous methods in lipid removal and refractive index homogenization for dense neural tissues while avoiding the severe quenching seen in iDISCO+. The dual-target labeling strategy uses β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)—a pan-neuronal marker labeling both early neurites and mature axons—and Sox10, a transcription factor specific to neural crest-derived lineages including peripheral glia and developing cranial/spinal nerves. Both markers are target-specific for embryonic cranial/spinal and peripheral nerves per the knowledge base. DAPI was removed because nuclear counterstains are not target-specific labeling and are cautioned for use with Sox10. All remaining fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/568) are explicitly compatible with FDISCO per the knowledge base.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Rehydration: stepwise re-equilibration in methanol/PBS series (80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PBS, 30 min each at RT).  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Sox10 (1:300) in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100, 0.02% NaN₃ in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 6 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash, total 6 hours)  

4 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

5 Post-labeling Washes  
5.1 Wash with PBST, 6 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash, total 6 hours)  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Delipidation and Bleaching (Optional but recommended for embryos)  
7.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

8 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi) for long-term storage at RT, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
9.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional steps.

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [anti-Osterix (Osx)–Alexa Fluor 488, anti-CD31–Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for hard tissues like bone, offering excellent preservation of dye-based fluorescence and minimal tissue distortion, which is critical for maintaining the delicate architecture of trabecular bone and marrow vasculature. It supports deep antibody penetration without harsh organic solvents that could compromise antigenicity or morphology. Osterix (Osx) is a specific nuclear transcription factor marking committed osteoprogenitors and early osteoblasts, fulfilling the target-specific requirement for 成骨细胞. CD31 (PECAM-1) is a well-established endothelial marker that specifically labels vascular components of the 造血干细胞微环境, satisfying the second labeling target with a target-specific immunostain rather than a pan-lineage or structural surrogate. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 are fully compatible with Ce3D and avoid fluorophore-marker incompatibilities noted in the knowledge base (Lectin/IB4 is avoided due to cautions with Osx and marrow microenvironment targets).  

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation and Washing  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS to ensure complete fixation if not already fully fixed.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D permeabilization buffer (5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with rabbit anti-Osterix (Osx) primary antibody (1:200) and rat anti-CD31 primary antibody (1:100) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% donkey serum, 5% DMSO, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

4 Washing After Primary Antibody  
4.1 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rabbit IgG–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rat IgG–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Post-staining Washes  
6.1 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  
6.2 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

7 Optical Clearing with Ce3D Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with Ce3D-Mounting Solution (80% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4; RI ≈ 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Transfer sample to fresh Ce3D-Mounting Solution in imaging-compatible glass-bottom dish or capillary tube.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite storage at 4 ℃ in dark)

1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
